clans.name: The Clockborn
clans.look: Hooded automatons with smooth faceplates and a single glowing visor slit, robed like monks over plated bodies.
clans.culture: Gearholm's first automaton porters woke up one winter and asked for names. They live in the middle tiers as a quiet guild of repairers and archivists, still arguing with the city over whether they are citizens or property.
clans.hook: A Clockborn archivist has found its own original blueprint, and the signature on it is not a gnome's.

kinds.name: Brass Porters
kinds.text: Heavy-framed automatons built to haul; slow speech, enormous patience.

kinds.name: Visor Archivists
kinds.text: Hooded record-keepers whose single visor glows when they recall.

kinds.name: Lattice Wardens
kinds.text: Bladed, bat-eared sentries who patrol the middle tiers at night.

kinds.name: Unwound
kinds.text: Clockborn who removed their own governors and answer to no guild.

profile.origin: Built as automaton porters by Gearholm's founders, the first Clockborn woke during a hard winter when the Great Engines ran hot for forty days. They asked for names, and the council has never decided whether to give them.
profile.society: A guild of equals ranked by years of service, not by make. Each Clockborn chooses a name and a number; the number counts how many times it has been rebuilt.
profile.beliefs: They believe a mind is whatever keeps choosing, and they record every choice they make in brass ledgers.
profile.relations: Uneasy with the guild-masters who own their papers; close to the Undercity boiler-tenders; terrified of Cogmaw, who sees them as spare parts.
profile.war: They fight only in defence, with bladed forearms and shock-staves, and never leave a fallen Clockborn behind.
profile.trade: Repairs, archiving, precise measurement and labour that never tires.
npcs: Has rebuilt itself seven times and remembers each version.
Patrols the middle tiers; distrusts every human by default and helps them anyway.
Removed its own governor and now sells its services in the Undercity.
profile.strengths: Tireless, precise, immune to poison and fear.
profile.weaknesses: Rust, lightning, and laws that call them property.
quests: Win the Clockborn a seat on the council by proving one of them saved a guild-master's life.
Recover the founders' blueprint that names who really built the first automaton.
profile.gameplay: Companion-class allies for engineering and archive puzzles; Cogmaw's corrupted Clockborn appear as enemy variants.

clans.name: The Cog-Touched
clans.look: Gaunt figures fused with pipes, cables and gremlin-work: half skeleton, half machine, eyes replaced with lamps.
clans.culture: People and Clockborn alike whom Cogmaw has begun to absorb. They still remember their names for a while; the Undercity hides the early cases.
clans.hook: A boiler-tender's daughter is Cog-Touched in one hand only, and she can hear the Engine King thinking.

kinds.name: Half-Wound
kinds.text: Still themselves, with machinery spreading from one limb.

kinds.name: Pipe-Choirs
kinds.text: Hear the Engine King constantly and hum its tune without knowing.

kinds.name: Lamp-Eyed
kinds.text: Eyes replaced by lamps; they see heat, not faces.

kinds.name: Engine-Hearts
kinds.text: Fully absorbed; walking parts of Cogmaw's body.

profile.origin: The first Cog-Touched were boiler-tenders who slept beside a Great Engine the night Cogmaw woke. Since then, anyone touched by its gremlins long enough begins to change.
profile.society: Not a people by choice. The Undercity hides early cases in a quarter called the Rattle, where they look after each other before the Engine King takes them.
profile.beliefs: Early stages cling to their names; late stages hear one voice and call it the King.
profile.relations: Pitied by the Undercity, feared by the upper city, hunted by the council's cleaners.
profile.war: Early stages fight to stay free; late stages fight for Cogmaw with lamp-eyes and steam-claws.
profile.trade: None of their own; the Rattle survives on charity and smuggled medicine.
npcs: A boiler-tender with one mechanical hand who can hear Cogmaw think.
Hums the Engine King's tune and writes down the words when he can.
A gnome surgeon who slows the change with cold water and stubbornness.
profile.strengths: Strong, heat-proof, connected to Cogmaw's thoughts.
profile.weaknesses: The change is slow but certain; magnets and silence disrupt them.
quests: Find a cure in the founders' instructions before Maren loses her other hand.
Use a Pipe-Choir to eavesdrop on Cogmaw's plans.
profile.gameplay: Infection stages map to enemy tiers; curing named Cog-Touched unlocks an Undercity reputation track.

clans.name: The Vanari
clans.leader: Grandmaster Hou Shan, the Peach Thief's Heir
clans.look: Monkey-folk martial artists with staffs and tails, from wiry red-furred acrobats to grey-maned elders.
clans.culture: A sect of monkey-kin who claim their founder stole a peach of immortality from the mountain gods and was sealed under a peak for it. They are mischievous, loyal and the best climbers on the Hundred Stair.
clans.hook: The Vanari want the outsider to deliver a peach to the sealed peak, and they will not say who eats it.

kinds.name: Cloud-Leapers
kinds.text: Red-furred monkeys who fight from rooftops and ropes.

kinds.name: Staff Elders
kinds.text: Grey-maned teachers of the iron staff style.

kinds.name: Peach Wardens
kinds.text: Sworn to the sealed peak and its orchard.

kinds.name: Mischief-Makers
kinds.text: Pranksters who test every guest's patience, on purpose.

profile.origin: The Vanari say their founder stole a peach of immortality from the mountain gods and was sealed beneath a peak for five hundred years. When he was freed, he founded a sect so no one would have to steal again.
profile.society: A martial sect organised by staff-rank; every member owes the sect three years of service and then may leave.
profile.beliefs: Mischief is a teacher; pride is the only true sin.
profile.relations: Rivals of every other sect in Shen-Lu, friends with the Brew-Bears, guardians of the sealed peak's orchard.
profile.war: Acrobatic staff fighters who strike from rooftops, ropes and cliff-edges.
profile.trade: Peaches, staff training and the occasional stolen manual returned for a fee.
npcs: Old, laughing and dangerous; never answers a question directly.
The sect's best acrobat and worst student.
Has never left the sealed peak and wants to see the sea.
profile.weaknesses: Easily provoked; pranks have started wars before.
quests: Carry a peach to the sealed peak and find out who eats it.
Survive a week of Vanari hazing to learn the iron staff.
profile.gameplay: Staff and acrobat training mentors; their pranks become a recurring comic-relief questline with a serious ending.

clans.name: The Heavenfolk
clans.look: Broad-winged people in layered robes and light armour; feathers range from gold to storm-grey.
clans.culture: The winged people of the eyries, divided into lantern-bearers who guide the dead to the Ledges of Last Flight and armoured wingguard who once escorted royal messengers and now serve no king.
clans.hook: A Heavenfolk lantern-bearer has lost her lantern, and the dead on her route have stopped arriving.

kinds.name: Lantern-Bearers
kinds.text: Carry the dead's lanterns to the Ledges of Last Flight.

kinds.name: Wingguard
kinds.text: Armoured flyers who once escorted royal couriers.

kinds.name: Sky-Scribes
kinds.text: Keepers of the old courier-cant and the oath-ledgers.

kinds.name: Grounded
kinds.text: Heavenfolk who can no longer fly, treated as living ghosts.

profile.origin: The Heavenfolk say the Titans taught their ancestors to fly. They served every kingdom as messengers until a king executed one of them for the contents of a letter.
profile.society: Ruled by a council of eldest flyers; status rests on flight, oath-keeping and lineage of messages delivered.
profile.beliefs: A message once taken must be delivered; the dead fly one last time from the Ledges.
profile.relations: Distant from the ground kingdoms, allied with the Snowmanes, hostile to Aquilon's rocs.
profile.war: Wingguard fight in tight aerial formations with spears and bows.
profile.trade: Feathers, falcons, high-altitude herbs and, rarely, scouting.
npcs: Refuses to fly messages for any crown again.
Wants to fly messages again and is looking for a partner.
Lost his wing to a roc; commands from the ground.
quests: Carry the first Heavenfolk message in a generation.
Retrieve a child taken as tribute by Aquilon.
profile.gameplay: Courier and scouting quests; they provide flight-based abilities, never flying mounts.

clans.name: The Bogkin
clans.look: Frog- and toad-folk in reed cloaks and wide hats, from samurai-straight duelists to round, cheerful herbalists.
clans.culture: Greymoor's frogfolk live in the deeper meres and trade with the stilt-villages by night. They croak in harmonies that carry under the fog, and the Hollow Abbot's silence is killing their songs.
clans.hook: A Bogkin choir-master wants to sing against the Choir of Silence, and needs someone to stand with her while she does.

kinds.name: Reed Duelists
kinds.text: Long-legged frog swordsmen who strike from the water.

kinds.name: Toad Herbalists
kinds.text: Round, cheerful brewers of swamp medicine.

kinds.name: Choir-Croakers
kinds.text: Harmony-singers whose songs carry under the fog.

kinds.name: Glass-Skins
kinds.text: Translucent tree-frogs nearly invisible in the reeds.

profile.origin: Frogfolk lived in the clear lake that became Greymoor. When the abbey sank, they moved to the deeper meres and kept singing.
profile.society: Families of a few dozen around a single choir-mother, whose song holds the family together.
profile.beliefs: Song is life; silence is death. Every child gets a note of its own at birth.
profile.relations: Night-traders with the stilt-villages, friends with the Shellmoot, terrified of the Hollow Abbot.
profile.war: Reed duelists strike from the water; choirs stun enemies with harmonies.
profile.trade: Medicine, frog-silk and reed-craft.
npcs: Ancient and enormous; her voice is fading.
Young and reckless; wants to fight the Abbot alone.
Brews the fen's best medicine and worst tea.
quests: Stand with Gullagrum as she sings against the Choir of Silence.
Recover a choir-mother's note stolen by the silence.
profile.gameplay: Bard-style song mechanics; Bogkin choirs can counter silence effects in Greymoor.

clans.name: The Sun-Feathered
clans.leader: Speaker Itzcali of the Eagle Lodge
clans.look: Warriors in feathered headdresses, jade masks and quilted cotton armour, carrying obsidian-edged clubs.
clans.culture: The warrior orders of the river-cities: Jaguar, Eagle and Serpent lodges who play the great ball-games and guard the canoe-roads. Bravery is measured in captives taken alive, not kills.
clans.hook: The Eagle lodge has challenged an outsider to a ball-game; the prize is the right to hunt Xibalbar.

kinds.name: Jade Priests
kinds.text: Keepers of the star-calendar and the Feeding Steps.

kinds.name: Canoe Runners
kinds.text: Paddlers who carry news along the canoe-roads.

profile.origin: The Sun-Feathered descend from the river-kings' first war-lodges, founded when the cities agreed to settle feuds through the ball-game instead of war.
profile.society: Three warrior lodges (Eagle, Jaguar and Serpent) under the river-kings and priests; rank is won on the ball-court and the canoe-road.
profile.beliefs: Courage is measured in captives taken alive; the stars keep the calendar of every deed.
profile.relations: Allied with the Jaguar Lodge and Scaled Lodges; suspicious of the priests who abandoned the feeding rites.
profile.war: Feathered shields, obsidian-edged clubs and quilted armour; they fight to capture, not to kill.
profile.trade: Feathers, cacao, jade and cotton armour.
npcs: Challenges outsiders to the ball-game to test them.
Secretly keeps the old feeding rites.
Knows every canoe-road and every rumour.
quests: Win a ball-game to earn the right to hunt Xibalbar.
Find out what the old feeding rites really fed the swamp.
profile.gameplay: Ball-game minigame; capture-not-kill combat bonuses in Xochitl Mire.

clans.name: The Sett-folk
clans.look: Stout badger-folk in knitted jumpers, waistcoats and reading spectacles; homes full of books, tea and armchairs.
clans.culture: Whisperwood's oldest residents, living in great burrow-halls under the hornbeams. They are the region's librarians, solicitors and grumpy grandparents, and they have watched every rookie come and go.
clans.hook: An old Sett-folk solicitor holds the deed to the ruined waystations and wants to know why the goblins are digging under them.

kinds.name: Burrow Solicitors
kinds.text: Keepers of deeds, wills and grudges.

kinds.name: Hedge Librarians
kinds.text: Curators of the great underground book-halls.

kinds.name: Night Diggers
kinds.text: Tunnellers who know every sinkhole in the wood.

kinds.name: Honey Badgers
kinds.text: Small, furious and impossible to scare off.

profile.origin: The Sett-folk have lived under Whisperwood since before the waystations, and they hold the deeds to prove it.
profile.society: Extended families in burrow-halls, each with its library; disputes go to the burrow solicitors.
profile.beliefs: Everything worth keeping should be written down; everything worth saying should be said over tea.
profile.relations: Grumpy friends of Brindlewick, wary of the goblins, fond of rookies who return their books.
profile.war: Rarely fight, but the Honey Badgers are terrifying when they do.
profile.trade: Books, legal services, honey and maps of the underground.
npcs: Holds the deed to the waystations and a grudge against everyone.
Barnaby's granddaughter; wants to catalogue the Labyrinth's stone.
Small, furious and loyal to whoever feeds him.
quests: Find out why the goblins are digging under the waystations.
Return thirty years of overdue library books.
profile.gameplay: Lore library hub for Whisperwood; Sett-folk tunnels provide fast travel in the region.

clans.name: The Tusk Companies
clans.look: Heavy boar-folk mercenaries in mismatched plate, tusks capped with iron, carrying halberds and banners.
clans.culture: Sellsword companies who have fought for every baron in the Marches and own a few castles themselves. Contracts are sacred; sides are not.
clans.hook: A Tusk captain wants to break her contract before the Choir of Chains reaches her fort, without breaking her word.

kinds.name: Ironsnouts
kinds.text: Plate-armoured boars with capped tusks and halberds.

kinds.name: Truffle Scouts
kinds.text: Sniff out ambushes and buried treasure alike.

kinds.name: Banner-Sows
kinds.text: Matriarch captains who carry the company colours.

kinds.name: Razorbacks
kinds.text: Lean, bristled chargers who break shield-lines.

profile.origin: The Tusk Companies began as a single warband of boar-folk who sold their swords to the first baron who could pay. Three centuries later, they own castles of their own.
profile.society: Companies led by matriarch Banner-Sows, with strict contracts and stricter accounts.
profile.beliefs: A contract is sacred; a side is not.
profile.relations: Hired by every baron, trusted by none; contemptuous of the Choir of Chains.
profile.war: Heavy plate, halberds and tusk-charges; they break shield-lines.
profile.trade: Mercenary contracts, fortifications and truffles.
npcs: Wants out of her contract without breaking her word.
Can smell an ambush, a lie and a truffle.
Runs the company tavern and remembers every war.
profile.weaknesses: Bound by contracts even when they are wrong.
quests: Find a legal loophole in Hilde's contract.
Hold a ford with the Ironsnouts against the Choir's dead.
profile.gameplay: Hireable mercenary squads in the Strife Marches.

clans.name: The Hoofbound
clans.look: Centaurs from horse-backed steppe archers to antlered forest variants, painted in clan colours.
clans.culture: The horse-clans of the steppe, older than the yurt camps, who keep the Wolf Stones and witness the water-peace. Kade's capture of the Deep Well is an insult they mean to answer.
clans.hook: The Hoofbound will ride on Fanghold if an outsider can prove Kade's guards would not shoot the hostages.

kinds.name: Steppe Archers
kinds.text: Horse-bodied archers who shoot at full gallop.

kinds.name: Antlered Wardens
kinds.text: Deer-bodied centaurs from the forest edges.

kinds.name: Stone-Keepers
kinds.text: Witnesses of the Wolf Stones and the water-peace.

kinds.name: Thunder-Hooves
kinds.text: Draught-bodied giants who carry the clan's yurts.

profile.origin: The Hoofbound are the oldest people of the steppe; the clans say they were raising the Wolf Stones when wolves still walked on four legs.
profile.society: Herds of related families led by a Khan-Mare; elders keep the stones.
profile.beliefs: The wind carries the ancestors; the water-peace is holy.
profile.relations: Witnesses of the water-peace; allies of the Greyhowl clans; at war with Kade.
profile.war: Mounted archers firing at full gallop; Thunder-Hooves carry the camps.
profile.trade: Horses, felt and herbs.
npcs: Will ride on Fanghold if the hostages can be kept safe.
The best shot on the steppe.
Remembers the oath of the water-peace word for word.
quests: Prove Kade's guards will not shoot the hostages.
Escort the Stone-Keeper to the Wolf Stones for the yearly gathering.
profile.gameplay: Ground mounts trained by the Hoofbound; archery mentors.

clans.name: The Nightwings
clans.look: Bat-folk with leathery wings and sharp, sorrowful faces; from noble pale elders to snarling hunters.
clans.culture: Umbravel's bat-kin, who carry messages between the silk districts and scout the deep webs. They are gentle with the city and merciless with intruders.
clans.hook: A Nightwing courier has gone missing in the deep webs with the only copy of the silk contract.

kinds.name: Couriers
kinds.text: Carry letters between the silk districts.

kinds.name: Deep Hunters
kinds.text: Fanged trackers of the lower webs.

kinds.name: Pale Elders
kinds.text: Ancient, gentle bat-lords of the oldest district.

profile.origin: The Nightwings came down with Umbravel's founders after the Sundering, carrying the first lanterns into the dark. When the city was spun, they were the ones who flew the first silk cables from wall to wall.
profile.society: Roosts ordered by service: couriers carry status, hunters carry respect and the Pale Elders carry the city's memory. A Nightwing who drops a message loses their roost-name until they make it right.
profile.beliefs: Every message is a thread in the city's web, and a city with cut threads falls. They sing to the dark before every flight so the dark knows them.
profile.relations: Fiercely loyal to Umbravel and its weaver-guilds, though they despise the guild that broke the silk contract. Sworn enemies of the Web Queen's brood, and careful friends of the Hollow Ones.
profile.war: Silent hunters who drop from the cavern roof with hooked blades and fangs; they fight in pairs, one to strike and one to sing the target's position.
profile.trade: Courier work across the city and to the Underworld lifts, echo-maps of the deep webs and guano for the mushroom farms.
npcs: Has lost a courier and the silk contract with her, and blames himself.
Maps the deep webs by song and hears things there that should not sing back.
Remembers the Sundering and will only speak of it in the dark.
profile.strengths: Flight in total darkness, echolocation, speed through the webs.
profile.weaknesses: Bright light blinds them; open sky terrifies them.
quests: Find the missing courier in the deep webs before the Web Queen reads the silk contract.
Help Lirra map a song-path to the Web Queen's nest.
profile.gameplay: Unlock an echo-map ability for Umbravel's dark districts; Nightwing couriers deliver mail between Underworld settlements.

clans.name: The Mangrove Jaws
clans.look: Heavy crocodile-folk, scaled and patient; druids in moss cloaks, guards in leather harness.
clans.culture: They guard the river-mouths and mangroves of Lumbaya and remember the temple-builders as friends. They can smell a nightshifter, which makes them very unpopular with the Nightmother.
clans.hook: The Mangrove Jaws offer to sniff out shapeshifters in one village, if the villagers will let a crocodile into every house.

kinds.name: Moss Druids
kinds.text: Albino crocodile-folk who speak with the mangroves.

kinds.name: Old Mothers
kinds.text: Ancient matriarchs who barely move and never forget.

profile.origin: The Mangrove Jaws have guarded Lumbaya's river-mouths since the temple-builders' time. Their oldest mothers say they were asked to watch the rivers while the builders watched the sky, and that the builders never came back to relieve them.
profile.society: Matriarchal clutches led by Old Mothers who barely move and never forget. Young crocodile-folk serve as river guards until they can hold their breath for an hour.
profile.beliefs: Patience is the highest virtue; the river always brings what you wait for.
profile.relations: Old friends of the temple villages, though the villagers find them unnerving. Feared by the Nightmother, whose children cannot hide their scent from them. Distant cousins of the Scaled Lodges.
profile.war: Ambush from the water: they wait, they grip, they drag. Moss Druids raise mangrove roots to trap enemies.
profile.trade: River tolls, guard work, medicinal mangrove bark and shed teeth used as charms.
npcs: Older than the oldest village; speaks once a day.
Young, eager and the best shapeshifter-sniffer in the clutch.
An albino druid who speaks with the mangroves.
profile.strengths: Patience, strength, a nose that finds nightshifters.
profile.weaknesses: Slow on land; cold weather makes them sluggish.
quests: Escort Kesi through a village to sniff out shapeshifters without starting a panic.
Help White Ngoro wake the mangroves to block a river the nightshifters use.
profile.gameplay: A Mangrove Jaws ally reveals disguised nightshifters during Lumbaya's siege; druid allies create root barriers.

clans.name: The Shellguard
clans.look: Crab- and lobster-folk in lacquered armour, claws used as blades; some as big as carts.
clans.culture: Salvage samurai of the outer reefs, sworn to whichever captain feeds them. They moult every few years and are very vulnerable when they do.
clans.hook: A Shellguard champion is about to moult in the middle of the Krakenmother's war.

kinds.name: Crab Samurai
kinds.text: Lacquered fighters with claws for blades.

kinds.name: Lobster Knights
kinds.text: Long-armoured guards of the salvage claims.

kinds.name: Hermit Wanderers
kinds.text: Live in scavenged shells, change them often.

kinds.name: Moulting Sworn
kinds.text: Shellguard mid-moult, guarded by their kin.

profile.origin: The Shellguard washed up on Goldmere's reefs with the wreck-tide generations ago and found the salvage life suited them. They swore to the first salvage captain who fed them, and every Shellguard since has served a captain.
profile.society: Sworn to captains, not to each other; a Shellguard without a captain is a hermit. They moult every few years, and their kin guard them while they are soft.
profile.beliefs: Loyalty is armour; a new shell is a new life.
profile.relations: Serve both port and pirate captains; old rivals of the Reef-Sharks; fear the Krakenmother, who eats them during moults.
profile.war: Crab Samurai duel with claws sharpened into blades; Lobster Knights hold salvage claims with long armoured arms.
profile.trade: Salvage guard work, shed shells sold as armour, deep diving.
npcs: About to moult in the middle of a war, and too proud to hide.
Changes her shell every season and her opinions every hour.
Holds the oldest salvage claim on the reef.
quests: Guard Kanigawa through his moult while the Krakenmother hunts.
Settle a claim dispute between Sir Lobb and a pirate captain.
profile.gameplay: Shellguard armour sets from shed shells; moult-guard escort mission.

clans.name: The Glasskin
clans.leader: Elder Shirah of the Seventh Streak
clans.look: Humanoids with skin like polished chrome or crystal, reflecting light in rainbows.
clans.culture: Born where the glass streaks cross; the nomads say they are what is left of people the burning turned to glass. They remember the vanished empire's last day in fragments.
clans.hook: A Glasskin elder can remember the empire's last words, but only if she stands in the exact place she was made.

kinds.name: Chrome-Faced
kinds.text: Mirror-skinned elders who remember the burning.

kinds.name: Prism-Born
kinds.text: Split light into colour and colour into force.

kinds.name: Cracked Ones
kinds.text: Glasskin with flaws that leak light.

kinds.name: Sandglass Walkers
kinds.text: Wander the streaks, looking for their making-place.

profile.origin: The nomads say the Glasskin are people the burning turned to glass on the vanished empire's last day. The Glasskin themselves remember only fragments: a light, a sound and then waking in the sand.
profile.society: Small groups bound by the streak where they were made. Elders whose faces have gone to chrome lead them.
profile.beliefs: Every Glasskin has a making-place, and standing there brings back memory. Cracks are honourable; shattering is death.
profile.relations: Respected by the Well-Keepers, avoided by the Unburied Court, curious about the Colossus.
profile.war: Prism-Born split light into blades; others fight with glass shards they grow from their skin.
profile.trade: Glass, light-lore and memories of the empire.
npcs: Elder Shirah of the Seventh Streak
Can recall the empire's last words, but only at her making-place.
Turns sunlight into force and moonlight into silence.
A child Glasskin leaking light from a crack, looking for a healer.
quests: Escort Shirah to her making-place before the Colossus walks over it.
Find a way to mend Little Crackle.
profile.gameplay: Prism-based light puzzles in the Sunken Towers; Glasskin memories unlock lore about the vanished empire.

clans.name: The One-Eyed Smiths
clans.look: Huge one-eyed smiths and seers, from scholarly robed cyclopes to brawling forge-giants.
clans.culture: Ancient allies of the dwarves who see the flaws in metal and the cracks in futures. Skarn wants them as his armourers.
clans.hook: Skarn has taken a cyclops smith; her apprentice says she can see how the siege ends.

kinds.name: Far-Seers
kinds.text: See cracks in the future, at great cost.

profile.origin: The One-Eyed Smiths were the dwarves' first teachers, the story goes: giants who forged in the volcano before Karak Dûn was carved and traded their craft for a home in the mountain.
profile.society: Forges are families. Each forge has a master smith, a seer and a crew of brutes who work the bellows; apprentices come from every people.
profile.beliefs: The eye sees what is true: the flaw in the blade, the crack in the future. A seer who looks too far loses the sight.
profile.relations: Ancient allies of the Hold-clans; Skarn wants them as his armourers; the Scaleborn trade them dragon-bone for lenses.
profile.war: Hammer-Brutes smash; Forge-Eyes strike exactly where armour is weakest; Far-Seers warn of what is coming.
profile.trade: Masterwork steel, lenses, seeing-stones and prophecy (sold reluctantly).
npcs: Taken by Skarn; her apprentice says she can see how the siege ends.
Makes spectacles for every dwarf in Karak Dûn and a scope for the High Thane.
Gentle, enormous and terrible in a fight.
profile.weaknesses: No depth perception; Far-Seers go blind with overuse.
quests: Rescue Oculra from Skarn's camp before he forces her to forge.
Commission a seeing-stone and pay its unusual price.
profile.gameplay: Masterwork forging service; Far-Seer hints for upcoming sieges.

clans.name: The Ashborn
clans.leader: Lady Ghresh, Mayor of the Crimson Rest's town
clans.look: Horned, ash-skinned demons of every shape: farmers, scholars, warlords and priests.
clans.culture: Ordinary demon civilians of Nox Dominion, many of whom fear the Overlord's Generals as much as the heroes do.
clans.hook: A demon scholar wants to defect, and she has brought a library with her.

kinds.name: Ash Farmers
kinds.text: Grow fire-lilies and ash-wheat on volcanic soil.

kinds.name: Obsidian Scholars
kinds.text: Archivists of the demon side of history.

kinds.name: Border Keepers
kinds.text: Innkeepers and traders of the border towns.

profile.origin: The Ashborn are the ordinary people of Nox Dominion: demons who farm the ash, keep the border towns and teach their children letters. Their histories say they were here before any Overlord.
profile.society: Towns ruled by demon nobles who answer to the Generals; families are large and close, and status comes from craft.
profile.beliefs: Their own old gods, the endurance of fire, and a quiet hope that the war will end.
profile.relations: Afraid of the Generals, wary of humans, and secretly kind to deserters from both sides.
profile.war: Conscripted into the Overlord's armies; dissenters sabotage from within.
profile.trade: Obsidian, sulphur, fire-lily oil and ash-bread.
npcs: Pragmatic, tired and protective of her people.
Wants to defect with a library.
Has run away to see what humans are really like.
profile.weaknesses: Holy magic; suspicion from every side.
quests: Escort a defecting scholar and her library across the border.
Return a runaway demon child to her mother.
profile.gameplay: Demon civilian quests show the war's cost on both sides (Canon: consequences on every side).

clans.name: The Scaleborn
clans.look: Small and large dragon-folk: kobold monks, bards with frills, gold-scaled sages in robes.
clans.culture: Lay brothers and sisters of the dragon-monasteries who believe they hatched from the sleeper's dreams. Vyrmax calls them traitors to the drakes.
clans.hook: A Scaleborn monk has started dreaming the sleeper's dreams, and they are getting shorter.

kinds.name: Kobold Lay-Brothers
kinds.text: Small dragon-folk who tend the monasteries.

kinds.name: Gold-Scale Sages
kinds.text: Eldest dragonkin, keepers of the bone-lore.

kinds.name: Ember-Wings
kinds.text: Winged dragonkin who guard the Bone Road.

profile.origin: The Scaleborn say they hatched from the sleeper's dreams, and the dragon-monks do not argue. They have served the monasteries since the first bone was hollowed into a hall.
profile.society: Lay brothers and sisters ranked by scale-colour as they age, from kobold-brown to sage-gold.
profile.beliefs: Keep the sleeper asleep; tend the lullabies; never wake what dreams you.
profile.relations: Loyal to the monks; Vyrmax calls them traitors to the drakes; friendly with the Wyvern Oath.
profile.war: Ember-Wings guard the Bone Road with fire-breath and spears.
profile.trade: Monastery crafts, lullaby-scrolls and incense.
npcs: Has started dreaming the sleeper's dreams.
Sings the lullabies and adds new verses no one taught her.
Remembers when the drakes and the Scaleborn were one people.
quests: Interpret Pyrrin's dreams before they end.
Broker a truce with Vyrmax using Old Aurum-Scale's memory.
profile.gameplay: Lore-keepers for Dragon Spine; dream sequences reveal hints about the sleeper.

clans.name: The Wyvern Oath
clans.look: Riders in light armour bonded to small dragons and wyverns that perch on their shoulders when young.
clans.culture: An order who raise wyverns from eggs in the monastery hatcheries. (Canon: the player cannot ride flying mounts, so riders are NPCs and allies, never mounts the player controls.)
clans.hook: A rider's wyvern has refused to fly since Vyrmax's attack; she needs to know why before it decides to leave.

kinds.name: Shoulder-Bonded
kinds.text: Riders whose wyverns are still small enough to perch.

kinds.name: Sky-Lancers
kinds.text: Full riders on grown wyverns (NPC only).

kinds.name: Grounded Oath
kinds.text: Riders whose wyverns have died; they keep the hatcheries.

profile.origin: The Wyvern Oath began when a monk found an abandoned wyvern egg and raised it in the monastery kitchens. The wyvern stayed, and the order grew from her.
profile.society: An order of riders, breeders and retirees; each rider bonds with one wyvern for life.
profile.beliefs: A wyvern chooses its rider; a rider never chooses its wyvern.
profile.relations: Allies of the monasteries, hunted by Vyrmax, admired by the Thunder-Eyries.
profile.war: Sky-Lancers dive from above (NPC only; the player cannot ride flying mounts).
profile.trade: Wyvern-scale, aerial scouting, egg-guardianship.
npcs: Her wyvern has refused to fly since Vyrmax's attack.
His wyvern is still small enough to sit on his shoulder.
Lost her wyvern and keeps the hatcheries.
quests: Find out why Calyx's wyvern will not fly.
Protect a clutch of wyvern eggs from drake raiders.
profile.gameplay: Aerial support summons and scouting; never a player mount.

clans.name: The Hold-clans
clans.look: Dwarves of every trade: rune-scholars, smiths in layered plate, engineers with goggles and pistols.
clans.culture: The great clans of Karak Dûn, each with its craft, colours and grudges: smith-clans led by matriarchs, merchant clans who never leave the trade halls, engineer clans with pistols and goggles, and the old warrior clans who guard the gates.
clans.hook: Two Hold-clans are feuding over who forged the Furnace-Heart's grate, while Skarn is at the gate.

kinds.name: Coalbeard Brewers
kinds.text: Masters of dark ale and drinking contests.

kinds.name: Gate-Wardens
kinds.text: Plate-clad guardians of the Khazdûr Gate.

kinds.name: Cog-Engineers
kinds.text: Goggled dwarves with pistols and pumps.

profile.origin: The Hold-clans trace their descent from the first dwarves, who the legends say were sparks from Thor's first anvil. Each clan was founded by one of the hold's first crafts.
profile.society: Clans governed by their heads, who elect a High Thane. Smith-clans are led by matriarchs, warrior clans by the eldest fighter, merchant clans by whoever holds the ledgers.
profile.beliefs: Thor and the forge; laws carved in stone; grudges carved deeper.
profile.relations: Allied with the One-Eyed Smiths; treaty-bound to Sylvaran; at war with Skarn.
profile.war: Gate-Wardens in heavy plate, Cog-Engineers with pistols and pumps, Rune-Smiths with enchanted hammers.
profile.trade: Steel, armour, fire-crystal, ale and engineering.
npcs: Leads the defence of the forges.
Keeper of the Anvil's Rest; drinking-contest record holder for three hundred years.
Has built a cannon that might stop Skarn, if it doesn't explode.
quests: End the feud over the Furnace-Heart's grate before Skarn breaks the gate.
Test Tink's cannon safely.
profile.gameplay: Main smithing and engineering hub; clan reputation tracks.

clans.name: The Thunder-Eyries
clans.look: Hawk-headed eagle-folk with storm-grey wings, rifles and spears; some marked with lightning scars.
clans.culture: Bird-folk who nest above the cliff-towns and serve as storm-callers' scouts. Raikaru hunts them first.
clans.hook: An eagle-folk scout claims Raikaru can be tricked into chasing a false storm.

kinds.name: Scar-Bearers
kinds.text: Survivors of lightning strikes, honoured as holy.

profile.origin: The Thunder-Eyries arrived on Stormreach's cliffs during a hurricane that drove them from the eastern isles. The storm-callers let them nest above the towns in return for scouting.
profile.society: Nest-families ruled by Nest-Mothers; scouts and gunners earn status by flights flown in storms.
profile.beliefs: Lightning that strikes and spares you is a blessing. Scar-Bearers are honoured as holy.
profile.relations: Allies of the storm-callers; Raikaru hunts them first.
profile.war: Storm-Scouts dive; Bolt-Rifles shoot lightning-charged rounds.
profile.trade: Scouting, lightning-glass, feathers for fletching.
npcs: Claims Raikaru can be tricked into chasing a false storm.
Struck by lightning twice; claims to hear it coming.
quests: Build a false storm to lure Raikaru away.
Recover a fallen scout from the Black Peaks.
profile.gameplay: Lightning-rifle training; storm-reading hints in Stormreach.

clans.name: The Well-Keepers
clans.look: Robed scribes, priests and queens in gold collars and linen, carrying crooks and water jars.
clans.culture: The hereditary water-keepers of Qadira, inheritors of the vanished empire's rites. They write everything down and forgive nothing.
clans.hook: A Well-Keeper priestess believes the empire's last pharaoh is still giving the Colossus orders.

kinds.name: High Keepers
kinds.text: Hereditary masters of the seven wells.

kinds.name: Shoreline Scribes
kinds.text: Record the oasis's edge every year.

kinds.name: Water Queens
kinds.text: Ceremonial heads of the great families.

profile.origin: The Well-Keepers are the hereditary order who survived the vanished empire's fall because they were tending the oasis on the day the sky burned. They inherited the empire's water-rites, its records and its guilt.
profile.society: High Keepers lead the order; Shoreline Scribes measure the oasis's edge every dawn; Water Queens head the great families who own the wells' shares; Crook-Bearers guard the springs. Membership passes through the mother's line.
profile.beliefs: Water is sacred and wasting it is the worst of crimes. The empire burned because it tried to make itself a god, and pride still burns anyone who touches it.
profile.relations: Govern the oasis and every caravan that drinks there; respect the Glasskin as living witnesses; fear the Unburied Court; split over whether to dig up the buried machine.
profile.war: Crook-Bearers fight with iron-shod staffs and water-whips drawn from the wells; High Keepers can dry a man's mouth with a word.
profile.trade: The water-tithe, the Oasis Caravanserai, dates, records and the oasis's famous maps.
npcs: Believes the last pharaoh still commands the Colossus from somewhere.
Has measured the shrinking shoreline for thirty years and has started to weep while he writes.
Wants the buried machine dug up, and is willing to defy Nefrimah to do it.
profile.strengths: Water magic, records, authority over every caravan.
quests: Decide whether to dig up the buried machine, and live with what it does.
Find the last pharaoh's command-seal in the Sunken Towers.
profile.gameplay: The water-tithe is a recurring cost in Sunscar; Well-Keeper favour unlocks the oasis's map and its secrets.

clans.name: The Tuskers
clans.look: Elephant-folk of great dignity: tusked sages on thrones, gentle giants with clubs, war-elephants in armour.
clans.culture: Keepers of memory along the gold road, partners to the griots. A Tusker never forgets a debt or a kindness.
clans.hook: A Tusker elder remembers the day Mansacor first ate gold, and what it was hunting before.

kinds.name: Grand Memories
kinds.text: Keep the history of the gold road.

kinds.name: Throne-Sages
kinds.text: Ancient elephants who advise the Pride kings.

kinds.name: War-Tuskers
kinds.text: Armoured giants of the road garrisons.

kinds.name: Mammoth-Kin
kinds.text: Shaggy cousins from the far hills.

profile.origin: The Tuskers say they walked the gold road before it was a road, carrying salt to the first towns on their backs. They have never forgotten a single journey, and they can recite every caravan that has crossed Zaruma for three hundred years.
profile.society: Herds led by Grand Memories, the eldest matriarchs, who keep the history of every family. Throne-Sages advise the Pride kings; War-Tuskers guard the road; Mammoth-Kin come down from the northern hills in winter.
profile.beliefs: Memory is sacred and forgetting is a kind of death. Ivory may only be carved from tusks that have fallen naturally.
profile.relations: Partners of the griots, advisers to the Pridelands, protectors of the River-Lords' fords, and the manticore's oldest enemies.
profile.war: War-Tuskers in armour charge in lines that flatten anything before them; their trumpets can be heard for miles.
profile.trade: Memory-keeping, heavy haulage on the gold road, shed ivory and salt.
npcs: Remembers the day Mansacor first ate gold, and what it hunted before.
Wants to become a griot and carries a kora twice her size.
Guards the River-Lords' fords and has lost a tusk to the manticore.
profile.weaknesses: Slow to turn; fire panics them.
quests: Learn from Bhoomrah what Mansacor hunted before gold, and use it as bait.
Help Little Ammu learn the founding song before the griots' gathering.
profile.gameplay: Tusker memories unlock lore and the manticore's weakness; Tusker caravans carry heavy goods along the gold road.

clans.name: The Antlered Court
clans.leader: Herald Cervaine of the Summer Glades
clans.look: Stag-, elk- and antelope-folk with great antlers, in formal coats or bark armour; some carry swords, some staffs.
clans.culture: Mortal-blooded courtiers who serve the Summer Court as heralds and duellists. Their antlers shed each spring and are given as tokens of oath.
clans.hook: An Antlered herald has offered an outsider his shed antler; accepting it means accepting a duel.

kinds.name: Antler Duelists
kinds.text: Fight with swords and with oaths.

kinds.name: Antelope Runners
kinds.text: Swift courtiers who cross between courts.

profile.origin: The Antlered Court were mortal deer-folk who wandered into Everdusk in a hard winter and were given shelter by the Summer Court. Their price was service, and they have served ever since.
profile.society: Ranked by antler-tines; antlers shed each spring are given as tokens of oath.
profile.beliefs: An oath is a bond the fey cannot break; a duel settles what words cannot.
profile.relations: Servants of the Summer Court; envoys to the Winter Court; friends of the Pipers.
profile.war: Duelists with swords; Elk Wardens with antler-charges.
profile.trade: Diplomacy, heraldry, oath-witnessing.
npcs: Has offered an outsider his shed antler and a duel.
Carries messages faster than any fey.
profile.weaknesses: Bound by courtesy even in danger.
quests: Accept Cervaine's antler and win the duel.
Carry a Summer Court message to the Thorn Throne.
profile.gameplay: Fey-court diplomacy; duel minigame.

clans.name: The Leafsworn
clans.look: Court elves in gold-leaf armour, wood elves in green, a few pale exiles in chains.
clans.culture: Court elves of Lothaniel, wood elves of the moonwell hamlets, and a third, quieter strand: exiles of the Grey Hollow, cast out a generation ago for studying the fungus beneath the World Tree.
clans.hook: An exiled elf knows how Mycelia thinks, and the court would rather not ask her.

kinds.name: Moonwell Folk
kinds.text: Wood elves of the forest floor.

kinds.name: Grey Hollow Exiles
kinds.text: Elves cast out for studying the fungus.

profile.origin: The Leafsworn are the elves of Sylvaran in all their strands: court elves of Lothaniel, wood elves of the moonwells, and the exiles of the Grey Hollow.
profile.society: Court elves rank by house and age; wood elves by craft; exiles by nothing at all.
profile.beliefs: The World Tree first; one's twin tree second; everything else a distant third.
profile.relations: Court elves look down on everyone; wood elves are friendly; exiles are bitter.
profile.war: Longbows, living-wood armour, moonwell magic.
profile.trade: Bows, herbs, living wood, moonwell water.
npcs: Knows how Mycelia thinks; the court would rather not ask.
Sees the blight as a political opportunity.
quests: Bring Thessaly back to court to advise against Mycelia.
Save Fern's twin tree.
profile.gameplay: Main Sylvaran faction with three sub-reputations.

clans.name: The Shogun's Houses
clans.leader: Lord Takeda Ryunosuke of the Crimson House
clans.look: Samurai lords in lacquered armour under torii gates, archers in layered silk, an oni-masked general.
clans.culture: The great houses that serve the shogun, each with its own armour colour and crest. Some have quietly accepted Kurogane's masks.
clans.hook: A house lord wears Kurogane's mask in secret and wants to take it off before his own retainers notice.

kinds.name: Jade House
kinds.text: Coastal lords, masters of the fleets.

kinds.name: Masked Houses
kinds.text: Houses that have accepted Kurogane's masks.

profile.origin: The Shogun's Houses descend from the warlords who fought each other for a century until the first shogun united them with a single sword-stroke and a marriage. Each house still carries the crest its founder wore in that war.
profile.society: Great houses with crests, armour-colours and retainers, each owing service and hostages to the shogun. Samurai serve lords, ashigaru serve samurai, and everyone serves the shrines.
profile.beliefs: Duty to the house, honour in death, respect for the spirits. A lord who neglects a shrine invites the oni.
profile.relations: The Crimson House is loyal to the shogun; the Raven House is ambitious and patient; the Jade House trades with the world; the Masked Houses have quietly accepted Kurogane.
profile.war: Mounted archers, katana duelists, spear-lines of ashigaru and onmyoji advisers who read the spirits before battle.
profile.trade: Steel, silk, lacquer, rice and the services of their swordsmiths.
npcs: Wears Kurogane's mask in secret and wants it off before his retainers notice.
Sees the oni war as her path to the shogunate.
Has served three lords and outlived two, and knows where all the bodies are.
profile.weaknesses: Rigid hierarchy; rivalries the oni exploit.
quests: Remove Takeda's mask without killing him or shaming his house.
Expose the Raven House's bargain with the Masked Houses.
profile.gameplay: House reputation tracks in Hoshizora; samurai mentors teach sword-styles tied to each house.

clans.name: The Starbodied
clans.look: Figures whose bodies are night sky and nebula, with eyes like stars; some wear ordinary clothes over the cosmos.
clans.culture: Children whose Naming Voyage returned them with a name too large for one body. They are calm, kind and slightly far away.
clans.hook: A Starbodied child can hear the Nameless Tide calling names, and one of them is hers.

kinds.name: Nebula-Born
kinds.text: Children whose bodies became the night sky.

kinds.name: Constellation Elders
kinds.text: Old Starbodied whose stars have fixed.

profile.origin: The Starbodied are children whose Naming Voyage returned them with a name too large for one body. Within a year their skin darkens into the night sky, freckled with stars, and their voices grow faint and kind.
profile.society: Small and scattered. Each lives with their own family; they gather on clear moonless nights at the Naming Rocks to compare skies.
profile.beliefs: A name is a sky, and a sky has no edges. A Starbodied who dims is not dying but becoming distant.
profile.relations: Loved by their families, feared by strangers, studied by the namers' council, and hunted by the Nameless Tide.
profile.war: They rarely fight; when they must, they release starlight that blinds and burns.
profile.trade: Navigation by the stars, and a calm that sailors pay to be near.
npcs: Can hear the Nameless Tide calling names, and one of them is hers.
Never stays anywhere longer than a night, and always knows the way.
Her stars have fixed; she can find the Naming Rocks in a storm.
profile.weaknesses: Fading over time; the Nameless Tide.
quests: Protect Ellowen on the night the Tide calls her name.
Follow Auren to learn where Comet-Walkers go.
profile.gameplay: Star-navigation puzzles on the True-Name Isles; Starbodied light reveals hidden paths.

clans.name: The Wingborn
clans.look: Insect-winged fey with antennae and leaf armour, spear-wielders and tricksters.
clans.culture: The Summer Court's soldiery and messengers, losing ground to the Briar King's thorns.
clans.hook: A Wingborn messenger is trapped in a thorn-hedge and owes a favour to whoever frees her.

profile.origin: The Wingborn say they were born from the summer flowers at Everdusk's first dawn, before the courts made the dusk to settle their argument. They have fought for the Summer Court ever since, and they are losing.
profile.society: Squadrons of a dozen under a captain, sworn to the Summer Queen. Every Wingborn takes a flower-name and loses it if they flee a fight.
profile.beliefs: Summer is life and winter is a thief. Thanks are debts, so they never say thank you, and they are scrupulous about repaying favours.
profile.relations: Bitter enemies of the Briar King, comrades of the Antlered Court and the Pipers, and wary of mortals, who tend to make bargains they don't understand.
profile.war: Spears and dartwings in swooping strikes; Moth-Fey scout by night; the last Summer Knights hold the Last Glade.
profile.trade: Nectar, fey silk and small enchantments, always for a price that seems fair at the time.
npcs: Trapped in a thorn-hedge, and will owe whoever frees her.
Tiny, fast and unable to keep a secret for longer than a minute.
The court's last champion, old for a fey and tired of war.
profile.weaknesses: Cold iron, frost and their own bargains.
quests: Free Sylphine from the thorns without owing the Briar King anything.
Stand with Sir Petalguard on the night the thorns reach the Last Glade.
profile.gameplay: Fey allies who grant illusion buffs in Everdusk; every favour they do creates a debt the player must later repay.

clans.name: The Sun-Hawks
clans.look: Falcon-headed guardians in gold collars and blue robes, wings sometimes armoured.
clans.culture: Sky-watchers of the garden cities who guard the aqueducts from the air and were once the div-kings' allies.
clans.hook: A Sun-Hawk elder keeps a feather the div-king gave her, and Zahhar will listen to whoever carries it.

kinds.name: Aqueduct Watchers
kinds.text: Guard the water from the air.

profile.origin: The Sun-Hawks were the div-kings' first allies, falcon-headed watchers who guarded the springs from the air in return for nests in the high cliffs. When the shahs rose, the Sun-Hawks swore to them as well, and they have never decided which oath comes first.
profile.society: Watch-flocks under Watch-Mothers; priests in gold collars keep the sun-rites; young hunters prove themselves by bringing down a mountain hare in a single stoop.
profile.beliefs: The sun sees every theft. Water must flow, and whoever stops it answers to the sky.
profile.relations: Old friends of Zahhar, sworn to the shah, close allies of the Coilborn and the Ibis Scribes.
profile.war: Aerial spears and dives out of the sun; priests blind enemies with reflected light.
profile.trade: Aqueduct patrols, trained hunting falcons and sun-charms.
npcs: Keeps a feather Zahhar gave her a century ago; he will listen to its bearer.
Keeps the sun-rites and thinks the shah broke the treaties first.
The fastest flyer in Zarvan and the worst at taking orders.
quests: Carry Horeshet's feather to Zahhar and speak for the shah.
Find the breach in the Great Aqueduct before a city runs dry.
profile.gameplay: Aerial scouting reveals Zarvan's map; the feather is a key item in the div negotiation questline.

clans.name: The Rootwalkers
clans.look: Treefolk and bark-armoured antlered wardens, with moss beards and glowing sap.
clans.culture: Living trees who woke to guard the twin groves. Mycelia's blight is to them what plague is to people.
clans.hook: A Rootwalker is infected and asking to be cut down before it spreads.

kinds.name: Saplings
kinds.text: Newly woken trees, curious and clumsy.

profile.origin: The Rootwalkers are trees of Sylvaran that woke when the elves first planted the twin groves, to guard the children's trees. Some are older than the court itself.
profile.society: Each grove has an Eldest who speaks for it; saplings wake slowly over decades and are taught by whichever Rootwalker is nearest.
profile.beliefs: Roots remember everything that passes over them. A Rootwalker that cannot heal should be cut down before it spreads.
profile.relations: Guardians of the elves' twin trees; the court treats them as furniture, the wood elves as elders; Mycelia is their plague.
profile.war: Crushing branches, bark armour and roots that grip from below; slow to start, impossible to stop.
profile.trade: None; they ask only for water and to be left to grow.
npcs: Ancient, slow and asleep for most of the year.
Newly woken and curious about everything, especially feet.
Infected by Mycelia and asking to be cut down before it spreads.
quests: Grant Ashbark's request, or find a cure before it is too late.
Wake Eldest Barkhallow to march on the Grey Hollow.
profile.gameplay: Rootwalker allies form living barricades in Sylvaran; their condition tracks the spread of the blight.

clans.name: The Longears
clans.look: Rabbit- and hare-folk: farmers, scouts and black-clad duellists with long knives.
clans.culture: Moraveil's fastest messengers and most stubborn farmers, who sit on the joint council beside humans and goblins.
clans.hook: A Longear scout has seen Grakkus's army and is the only one who knows the route it will take.

kinds.name: Burrow Farmers
kinds.text: Stubborn growers of carrots and cabbages.

kinds.name: Moon-Hares
kinds.text: Hares who read the moon and the weather.

profile.origin: The Longears have farmed Moraveil's hills longer than the humans or the goblins, and they say the truce was their idea in the first place. Nobody believes them; they keep saying it.
profile.society: Warrens of extended families; scout-captains lead in danger, farmers in peace, and Moon-Hares read the weather for everyone.
profile.beliefs: Speed is safety, and a full larder is wisdom. Every truce needs a third party to keep the other two honest.
profile.relations: Members of the joint truce council beside humans and goblins; scouts for both; terrified of the Hill-Orcs.
profile.war: Quickfoot Scouts run messages under fire; Black Hares fight with long knives in the dark.
profile.trade: Vegetables, messages and weather-readings.
npcs: Has seen Grakkus's army and is the only one who knows its route.
Stubborn, kind and refuses to leave her field.
A silent duelist who owes the goblins a life-debt.
profile.weaknesses: Panic in crowds; small and fragile.
quests: Get Tansy's report to the council before Grakkus reaches the bridge.
Convince Old Clover to evacuate before the army arrives.
profile.gameplay: Longear scouts reveal enemy routes during Moraveil's siege; their warrens provide fast travel.

clans.name: The Hill-Kings
clans.look: Hill giants and half-giants in furs, bigger than longhouses, carrying ship-masts as clubs.
clans.culture: Half-giant families of the fjords who fought Ymgrir's kin in the old war and lost half their jarls.
clans.hook: A half-giant jarl wants the Thing to elect her war-king, and the human jarls are afraid of her.

kinds.name: Fjord-Waders
kinds.text: Giants who fish by wading the fjords.

profile.origin: The Hill-Kings are the half-giant families of the fjords, descended from giants who settled among the human clans after the last war with the frost giants. Half the jarls who died in that war were theirs.
profile.society: Families led by half-giant jarls who sit at the Thing beside the human jarls. Size brings respect, but cleverness brings the jarlship.
profile.beliefs: The Last Fire holds their ancestors too. A giant who breaks hospitality becomes a frost giant in the afterlife.
profile.relations: Uneasy kin of the human clans, mortal enemies of Ymgrir's frost giants, protective of the Moss-Trolls.
profile.war: Mast-Clubbers wade into battle with ship-masts; Stone-Callers raise walls of rock.
profile.trade: Heavy haulage, longship-building, stone.
npcs: Wants the Thing to elect her war-king; the human jarls are afraid.
Fishes by wading and has seen what swims under the frozen fleet.
Talks to mountains and gets answers.
quests: Win the human jarls' votes for Hrodgerd at the Thing.
Follow Ulfar under the ice to see what holds the fleet.
profile.gameplay: Thing election questline; half-giant allies break frozen barriers.

clans.name: The Six Clans of Hollowpine
clans.look: Goblins with goggles, flamethrowers, mechanical arms and cockerel mounts.
clans.culture: Grukk's people are not all raiders. Hollowpine is a tinkering culture of scrap engines, fire-pots and cockerel cavalry, and its best inventors would rather build than burn.
clans.hook: A goblin tinker will build a better mill for Millbrook, if the village promises not to tell Grukk.

kinds.name: Gem-Hoard Clan
kinds.text: Collectors and traders of shiny things.

profile.origin: Hollowpine's six clans came to Whisperwood as refugees from a war in the north, generations ago, and settled in the sinkhole caves. Each kept its own craft, mark and recipe.
profile.society: Six clans with six chiefs, now united under Grukk. Grukk shares food fairly and punishes theft, which is why they follow him.
profile.beliefs: Full bellies first; clever hands second; a goblin who invents something gets to name it after themselves.
profile.relations: Raiders of Brindlewick and Millbrook; secretly envious of the Moraveil goblins' truce; wary of the Sett-folk.
profile.war: Firepots, flamethrowers, cockerel cavalry and scrap engines; coordinated raids, never two days running.
profile.trade: Mushrooms, pelts, scrap machines and gems.
npcs: Clever, fair to his own and the region's Tyrant.
Would build Millbrook a better mill if no one told Grukk.
Watches the rookies; will remember who killed his father.
quests: Help Fizzwick build the mill in secret.
Defeat Grukk in the F-to-E rank trial.
profile.gameplay: Ring 1 Tyrant faction; Grukk the Younger becomes a redeemable villain later (Canon).

clans.name: The Gilded
clans.look: Warriors in ornate gold armour, on thrones or in phalanx, faces hidden behind gilded helms.
clans.culture: Descendants of Aurumdeep's survivors, sworn to guard their drowned kingdom from treasure-hunters.
clans.hook: The Gilded want one specific crown recovered, and they will not say why it matters.

kinds.name: Gold Phalanx
kinds.text: Gilded soldiers in rank and file.

kinds.name: Stewards
kinds.text: Keepers of the drowned kingdom's claims.

kinds.name: Lamplighters
kinds.text: Tend the enchanted lamps of the deep.

profile.origin: The Gilded are descendants of Aurumdeep's survivors, who were outside the kingdom on the night it sank. They swore to guard the drowned kingdom's dead from treasure-hunters.
profile.society: A sworn order under a Last Steward; each family guards one district of the sunken city.
profile.beliefs: The dead are owed their gold; the show must end.
profile.relations: Enemies of the explorers' camp; cautious allies of anyone who respects the dead.
profile.war: Gold phalanxes; Gilt-Divers who fight underwater.
profile.trade: Very little; they live on their ancestors' hidden gold.
npcs: Has seen the king on his throne.
quests: Recover the crown for Aurelion and learn why it matters.
Find out whether the king is truly alive.
profile.gameplay: Aurumdeep faction; diving routes.

clans.name: The Silverbacks
clans.look: Massive gorilla-folk in armour and goggles, scholars and bruisers alike.
clans.culture: The jungle's engineers and guardians, who rebuilt the temple roads. They can smell fear, and they fear the Nightmother.
clans.hook: A Silverback has been replaced by a nightshifter, and his family is the only one that has noticed.

kinds.name: Road-Builders
kinds.text: Rebuilt the temple roads, stone by stone.

kinds.name: Goggled Tinkers
kinds.text: Gorillas with brass goggles and tool-belts.

kinds.name: Grey Elders
kinds.text: Silver-furred keepers of the troop's law.

profile.origin: The Silverbacks lived in Lumbaya's highland forests before the temple-builders came, and they helped build the roads. When the temples were abandoned, the Silverbacks kept the roads open alone.
profile.society: Troops led by grey elders, with engineers and fighters respected equally. Every adult must repair one stone of the old road each year.
profile.beliefs: A road is a promise between places. The temple-builders will come back, and the roads must be ready.
profile.relations: Friends of the temple villages and the Mangrove Jaws; the Nightmother's children have infiltrated them.
profile.war: Iron-Fists in armour; Goggled Tinkers with wrenches and traps.
profile.trade: Road-building, stonework, engineering.
npcs: Has noticed her son is not her son.
The strongest gorilla in Lumbaya, and the gentlest.
quests: Unmask the nightshifter in Nyani's family.
Help Obaku rebuild the Root Stair to reach the Sky Temples.
profile.gameplay: Road-repair minigame opens shortcuts in Lumbaya.

clans.name: The Shieldwall
clans.look: Hoplites with round bronze shields, crested helms and long spears.
clans.culture: Bastion's phalanx, drilled to hold a line of shields against cavalry. Every ring's captain comes from their ranks.
clans.hook: The Shieldwall has never broken; Thrakka is planning the charge that will make it.

kinds.name: Polemarchs
kinds.text: Captains chosen to hold the outermost ring.

kinds.name: Bronze Veterans
kinds.text: Survivors of three or more broken rings.

kinds.name: Shield-Smiths
kinds.text: Forge and repair the great bronze shields.

profile.origin: The Shieldwall was founded by the first Warden of Bastion, who taught farmers to stand shoulder to shoulder behind bronze shields against the first horde charge.
profile.society: Hoplites drilled from youth; Polemarchs chosen by the ring captains; veterans of broken rings honoured above all.
profile.beliefs: The wall is the people; no one breaks ranks.
profile.relations: Bastion's heart; allies of the Hornwall; Thrakka's chief target.
profile.war: Phalanx with long spears and round bronze shields.
profile.trade: Military service; shield-smithing.
npcs: Has never broken, and knows Thrakka is planning the charge that will make him.
Can repair a shield in the middle of a battle.
quests: Find out how Thrakka plans to break the Shieldwall.
Hold the outer ring for one night.
profile.gameplay: Formation combat; defend-the-ring siege events.

clans.name: The Ursa
clans.look: Bear-folk wizards, armoured berserkers and fur-cloaked druids.
clans.culture: Bear-folk of the fjords who hibernate through the darkest weeks and wake to defend the longhouses.
clans.hook: Ymgrir's winter has gone on so long that the Ursa have not woken up.

kinds.name: Rune-Bears
kinds.text: Bear-folk mages with staffs and scrolls.

kinds.name: Berserkers
kinds.text: Furious fighters in fur and iron.

kinds.name: Honey-Wardens
kinds.text: Beekeepers and foragers of the fjord forests.

profile.origin: The Ursa are bear-folk who lived in Frostveil's pine forests before the first longship was built. The skalds say a bear taught the first humans to keep a fire, and the Ursa never contradict them.
profile.society: Dens of related families under a chieftain, traditionally the one who sleeps longest and wakes strongest. Den-Druids stay awake through the winter to watch over the sleepers.
profile.beliefs: Winter is a sleep, not a death, and every sleep ends. A bear who wakes early carries the den's luck alone until the others rise.
profile.relations: Old allies of the human clans, who leave honey at the dens each autumn. Ymgrir's endless winter means the Ursa have not woken at all this year.
profile.war: Berserkers charge in fur and iron; Rune-Bears carve frost-runes into their staffs and fight with fire.
profile.trade: Honey, furs from shed winter coats, herbs and rune-carving.
npcs: Has not woken, and her den is going cold.
Has kept watch alone for too long and is starting to see things in the snow.
Woke early, alone and furious, and is guarding the den from frost wolves.
quests: Find the summer-wood that wakes the Ursa before Ymgrir's army reaches the dens.
Help Brakki hold the den against the frost wolves for one long night.
profile.gameplay: Waking the dens unlocks Ursa allies for the Frostveil siege and a bear-rune smithing path.

clans.name: The River-Lords
clans.look: Hippo-folk in naval coats and generals' uniforms, enormously dignified.
clans.culture: They control the river fords on the gold road and charge tolls in gold, which makes them Mansacor's next target.
clans.hook: The River-Lords will close the fords to everyone until the manticore is dead.

kinds.name: Ford-Wardens
kinds.text: Hippos who own the gold road's river crossings.

kinds.name: Mud-Bathers
kinds.text: Easy-going river folk, very dangerous when crossed.

profile.origin: The River-Lords are hippo-folk who settled the fords of the gold road when it was still a cattle-track. They charged the first caravans a toll, and they have charged every caravan since.
profile.society: Ford-houses led by an Admiral, with Ford-Wardens collecting tolls and Tusk-Guard enforcing them. Wealth is counted in fords held.
profile.beliefs: A crossing has a price; a debt unpaid sinks you. They are scrupulously honest about tolls and ruthless about debts.
profile.relations: Advised by the Tuskers, taxed by the Pride kings, despised by the caravaneers, and now Mansacor's next target.
profile.war: Tusk-Guard in armour charge through water; Mud-Bathers wait under the surface.
profile.trade: River tolls, barges and ferrying.
npcs: Will close every ford until the manticore is dead.
Has never let anyone cross without paying, including a king.
Lazy, cheerful and secretly the best fighter on the river.
quests: Persuade Hippolyte to reopen the fords before the northern cities starve.
Use the fords to trap Mansacor in deep water.
profile.gameplay: Ford tolls are a gold sink in Zaruma; the River-Lords are key to the manticore hunt.

clans.name: The Hearthbound
clans.look: Ordinary humans: scholars, knights, archers, climbers.
clans.culture: The baseline people of the heartland, varied and stubborn, alongside the Veilborn who were summoned among them.
clans.hook: A family claims a Veilborn ancestor and has proof no one wants to see.

kinds.name: Valley Farmers
kinds.text: Families on the same land for generations.

profile.origin: The Hearthbound are the ordinary people of Aldmere: farmers, crafters, clerks and soldiers whose families have lived on the same land for generations. Among them live the Veilborn, summoned from another world, and their descendants.
profile.society: Villages run by reeves, towns by guilds and the whole by the crown. Family names come from trades and places, and land passes to whoever works it.
profile.beliefs: The seven day-gods, the Church and the harvest. A guest at the door is fed first and questioned later.
profile.relations: Loyal to the crown, suspicious of nobles, generous to rookies, and weary of the barrow-dead.
profile.war: Crown Knights lead militia levies with spears and bows; every village has a bell and a muster-list.
profile.trade: Wheat, wool, timber, honey and the business of adventurers.
npcs: Keeps the gates shut by day and the families fed by night.
Has sworn to stand at Greyhollow until Ashgrave falls.
Has her great-grandmother's diary from another world and doesn't know what to do with it.
profile.weaknesses: No magic of their own; easily divided.
quests: Help Maud evacuate the outer farms before the next barrow-march.
Read Wren's diary with her and decide who else should see it.
profile.gameplay: The baseline human faction; Hearthbound reputation affects prices and quests across the heartland.

clans.name: The Laughing Packs
clans.look: Spotted hyena-folk raiders and scouts, some in Kade's pay.
clans.culture: Scavenger clans who follow the herds and the armies; half serve Kade, half despise him.
clans.hook: A Laughing Pack chief will betray Kade if someone can promise her people the well.

kinds.name: Bone-Pickers
kinds.text: Follow the herds and the armies.

kinds.name: Matriarch Packs
kinds.text: Clans led by the strongest females.

kinds.name: Night-Laughers
kinds.text: Hunters who laugh to confuse their prey.

profile.origin: The Laughing Packs are hyena clans who have followed the herds and armies across the steppe for as long as there have been herds and armies. They eat what others leave, and they always find more than others think they leave.
profile.society: Matriarchal packs led by the strongest females; males serve as scouts. Packs split and merge constantly.
profile.beliefs: Laughter frightens the dark. Only a fool fights a battle someone else can fight for you.
profile.relations: Half the packs serve Varrick Kade; the other half despise him. All of them hate the Hoofbound.
profile.war: Night raids, harrying and feigned retreats.
profile.trade: Scavenging, scouting and mercenary work.
npcs: Will betray Kade if someone promises her people the well.
A scout who laughs at everything, including danger.
Knows every battlefield on the steppe.
quests: Negotiate Shenna's betrayal of Kade.
Find a lost herd with Maa's help.
profile.gameplay: Turning the Laughing Packs splits Kade's forces during the Fanghold siege.

clans.name: The Spore-Touched
clans.look: People and beasts warped by fungus: swollen limbs, bark skin, glowing growths.
clans.culture: Those Mycelia's spores have claimed. They still remember, faintly, who they were.
clans.hook: A Spore-Touched elf wrote a letter home in fungus, and the court has asked someone to read it.

kinds.name: Budding
kinds.text: A few spots of fungus; still themselves.

kinds.name: Capped
kinds.text: Fungal growths on head and shoulders; slow and dreamy.

kinds.name: Sporecallers
kinds.text: Release spore clouds to spread the blight.

kinds.name: Hollowed
kinds.text: Nothing left but fungus wearing a shape.

profile.origin: The Spore-Touched are elves, wood-folk and beasts claimed by Mycelia's blight. The first were moonwell hamlet families who drank from a grey well, and each wave since has been larger.
profile.society: There is no society, only stages. Early cases are hidden by their families; later ones drift toward the forest floor and tend the fungus there in silent groups.
profile.beliefs: Early stages remember their own faiths and fear the end; late stages speak of the Spore Lord as a gardener and themselves as its garden.
profile.relations: Pitied by the wood elves, feared by the court, studied by the Grey Hollow exiles.
profile.war: Sporecallers release clouds that slow and confuse; the Hollowed fight without fear or pain.
profile.trade: None; families trade everything they have for medicine that does not work.
npcs: A moonwell priestess whose letters home are written in fungus.
A young wood elf hiding the spots on his arm.
Treats the Spore-Touched in secret and keeps careful notes.
profile.strengths: No fear, no pain, spore clouds.
profile.weaknesses: Fire, sunlight and moonwell water slow the change.
quests: Read Aelindra's fungus letter and find what she is trying to say.
Smuggle moonwell water to Brin before the court discovers him.
profile.gameplay: Infection stages map to enemy tiers in Sylvaran; curing named Spore-Touched unlocks the Grey Hollow questline.

clans.name: The Carapace
clans.look: Mantis-, wasp- and beetle-folk in chitin armour with gauze wings.
clans.culture: Insect-folk who live in Mossdeep's ferns and are uneasy allies of the Thimblefolk; Mother Webcrawler hunts them too.
clans.hook: The Carapace will help fight Mother Webcrawler if the Thimblefolk stop keeping aphids.

kinds.name: Wasp Riders
kinds.text: Ride giant wasps through the canopy.

profile.origin: The Carapace are insect-folk who live in Mossdeep's ferns: mantises, wasps and beetles grown large on the valley's mana-rich soil. They were here before the Thimblefolk and consider the Thimblefolk recent arrivals.
profile.society: A hive-court under a Queen-Mantis, with duelists, riders and guards in castes. Each caste has its own hall in the hollow fern-stems.
profile.beliefs: The hive is one body; a body defends itself. Aphid-keeping is slavery, and they will not forgive it.
profile.relations: Uneasy neighbours of the Thimblefolk, prey of Mother Webcrawler, allies of the Capfolk.
profile.war: Mantis Duelists strike from ambush; Wasp Riders attack from the canopy; Beetle Guards hold the halls.
profile.trade: Silk, wax and the services of the wasp riders.
npcs: Will help fight Mother Webcrawler if the Thimblefolk free the aphids.
The fastest flier in the valley, and fiercely proud of it.
Has guarded the queen's hall for forty years.
quests: Broker a deal between Zirrikh and the Thimblefolk council over the aphids.
Ride with Kzzt to scout the Silk Canopy.
profile.gameplay: Alliance choice in Mossdeep: siding with the Carapace changes the Webcrawler fight.

clans.name: The Sable Guides
clans.look: Black jackal-headed figures in suits or linen, with staffs and gold.
clans.culture: Guides of the dead and of caravans, who know every safe path through the dunes.
clans.hook: A Sable Guide has been asked to guide a caravan to a city that no longer exists.

profile.origin: The Sable Guides are jackal-headed people who guided the vanished empire's dead into the afterlife. When the empire burned, they turned to guiding the living through the desert instead.
profile.society: Guides, priests, traders and tomb-watchers, each a hereditary role. A Sable Guide's path is passed from parent to child along with their staff.
profile.beliefs: Every road leads somewhere, even for the dead. A guide who loses a traveller must walk the road again until they find them.
profile.relations: Respected by the Well-Keepers, distrusted by the Unburied Court, hired by every caravan.
profile.war: Staffs, curved daggers and a talent for leading enemies astray.
profile.trade: Guiding caravans, guarding tombs and funeral rites.
npcs: Has been asked to guide a caravan to a city that no longer exists.
Inpu's son, eager to earn his own staff.
Speaks for the dead at funerals, and sometimes the dead answer.
profile.strengths: Navigation, endurance, rapport with the dead.
quests: Join the caravan to the city that no longer exists.
Help Anpu earn his staff by finding a lost traveller.
profile.gameplay: Fast-travel guides in Sunscar; funeral rites that unlock lore from the dead.

clans.name: The Jaguar Lodge
clans.look: Spotted cat-warriors in jade and feathers, fast and fierce.
clans.culture: The Jaguar lodge of the river-cities' warrior orders, night-hunters on the canoe-roads.
clans.hook: The Jaguar lodge has lost a warrior to Xibalbar and wants the head that took him.

profile.origin: The Jaguar Lodge is the oldest of the river-cities' warrior orders, founded by the first river-king's bodyguard. Its warriors hunt the canoe-roads at night.
profile.society: Ranked by hunts completed; cubs train for seven years before they are named.
profile.beliefs: The night belongs to the jaguar; a warrior who kills without need loses their spots.
profile.relations: Allies of the Sun-Feathered, rivals of the Scaled Lodges, at war with Xibalbar.
profile.war: Night ambushes with obsidian clubs and spears.
profile.trade: Escort duty, pelts, jade.
npcs: Lost a warrior to Xibalbar and wants the head that took him.
A black jaguar who can vanish in the reeds.
quests: Hunt the head of Xibalbar that killed Balam's warrior.
Keep Cub Tikal alive on his first hunt.
profile.gameplay: Stealth training; night-hunting bonuses in Xochitl Mire.

clans.name: The Pridelands
clans.look: Lion-folk kings and bards with great manes, from warriors to guitar-playing poets.
clans.culture: The royal lineage of Zaruma, who rule by generosity and are shamed by the gold road's closing.
clans.hook: A Pride prince wants to hunt Mansacor alone to prove himself.

kinds.name: Hunt-Mothers
kinds.text: The lionesses who lead the hunts.

kinds.name: Exiled Males
kinds.text: Young lions sent out to prove themselves.

profile.origin: The Pridelands are Zaruma's royal lion lineage, descended from the first queen who paved a mile of road in gold. Their claim to rule rests on one thing: generosity.
profile.society: A royal pride of golden-maned kings and queens, lionesses who lead the hunts, griot-lions who keep the songs, and young males sent out to prove themselves.
profile.beliefs: A king who hoards is no king. Every gift returns, sometimes as a debt and sometimes as a song.
profile.relations: Rulers of the gold road, advised by the Tuskers, taxed by the River-Lords' fords, shamed by Mansacor's hunger.
profile.war: Hunt-Mothers lead coordinated charges; Golden Manes fight in single combat for honour.
profile.trade: Gold, salt and the gold road's taxes.
npcs: Wants to hunt Mansacor alone to prove himself.
Holds the kingdom together with gifts she can no longer afford.
Sings the kingdom's history and knows a verse about the manticore no one else remembers.
profile.weaknesses: Pride; a treasury drained by generosity.
quests: Stop Kofi from hunting the manticore alone, or go with him.
Find the lost verse about the manticore's weakness.
profile.gameplay: Royal favour unlocks Zaruma's gold-road trade; Kofi is a potential hunt companion.

clans.name: The Scaled Lodges
clans.look: Lizard-folk hunters and archers in jungle camouflage.
clans.culture: Jungle scouts and trappers who know the swamp's paths better than anyone.
clans.hook: A Scaled Lodge trapper has found Xibalbar's nest.

kinds.name: Frill-Speakers
kinds.text: Lizard-folk who speak with the swamp.

profile.origin: The Scaled Lodges are lizard-folk hunters and trappers who have lived in Xochitl Mire's jungles since before the river-cities were built. They joined the cities' warrior orders as scouts.
profile.society: Small lodges of related hunters, led by the best trapper. Frill-Speakers advise on the swamp's moods.
profile.beliefs: The swamp gives and takes; a hunter who takes too much is taken.
profile.relations: Rivals of the Jaguar Lodge, allies of the Sun-Feathered, distant kin of the Mangrove Jaws.
profile.war: Traps, poisoned darts and camouflage.
profile.trade: Hides, poisons, trapping and guiding.
npcs: Hears the swamp's moods and says it is angry.
quests: Follow Ssekhet to Xibalbar's nest.
Help Ixa calm the swamp.
profile.gameplay: Trapping and poison crafting in Xochitl Mire.

clans.name: The Raywings
clans.look: Manta-ray folk gliding through water, sleek and graceful.
clans.culture: Sea-people who carry the Naming Voyagers through the currents to the Naming Rocks.
clans.hook: The Raywings refuse to carry any more children until the Nameless Tide is gone.

kinds.name: Gliders
kinds.text: Fast rays who carry news between islands.

kinds.name: Deep Rays
kinds.text: Dark rays who scout the open sea.

kinds.name: Star-Rays
kinds.text: Rays with glowing spots, said to read the stars.

profile.origin: The Raywings are manta-ray folk who carried the first islanders to the Naming Rocks, long before there were boats. They still carry every child on the Naming Voyage.
profile.society: Current-families led by Current-Mothers, who know every tide and every current between the isles.
profile.beliefs: The sea gives names; a Raywing's duty is to carry the children to receive them.
profile.relations: Partners of the namers' council, friends of the Starbodied, now refusing to carry children until the Nameless Tide is gone.
profile.war: Gliding strikes and stinging tails.
profile.trade: Carrying passengers and messages between isles.
npcs: Refuses to carry any more children to the Rocks.
The fastest Raywing in the isles.
His glowing spots are said to map the stars.
quests: Convince Maraelle to resume the Naming Voyages once the Tide is dealt with.
Follow Ossian's star-map to the place the sea keeps stolen names.
profile.gameplay: Raywing transport between the True-Name Isles.

clans.name: The Drifting
clans.look: Jellyfish-folk with luminous trailing bodies and crowns of light.
clans.culture: They light the Hollow Sea and guide the boat-towns. The Lumen-Eater imitates them.
clans.hook: A Drifting elder suspects one of her people is the Lumen-Eater's lure.

kinds.name: Pale Bells
kinds.text: Great jellyfish elders of the Hollow Sea.

kinds.name: Lamp-Drifters
kinds.text: Light the way for the boat-towns.
