profile.origin: The Drifting are jellyfish-folk who have lit the Hollow Sea since long before the first boat tumbled down the great waterfall. The boat-towns call them the lamps of the deep, and steer by them.
profile.society: Blooms of hundreds, each led by a Pale Bell, the oldest and largest of the bloom. Lamp-Drifters travel with the boat-towns; Stingers guard the blooms; the Crowned Drift are born rarely and treated as nobles.
profile.beliefs: Light is a gift to be given, never taken. To use light as a lure is the worst blasphemy they know.
profile.relations: Guides of the boat-towns, allies of the Inkwardens, and the Lumen-Eater's victims and unwilling models.
profile.war: Paralysing tendrils and sudden bursts of blinding light.
profile.trade: Guidance through the dark, glowing jelly used in lamps, and light itself.
npcs: Suspects one of her own bloom is helping the Lumen-Eater.
Guides the smallest boat-town and is in love with its navigator's songs.
Wears a crown of light and refuses to dim it, even when hunted.
quests: Find the traitor in Lumessa's bloom before another boat-town follows a false light.
Guide a boat-town past the False Light with Flicker.
profile.gameplay: Drifting light-guides are the Hollow Sea's navigation system; a betrayal questline reveals the Lumen-Eater's lure.

clans.name: The Lagoon Folk
clans.look: Merfolk with fins, tridents and coral crowns; some with octopus hair.
clans.culture: The sea-elves and merfolk of Lirian's outer lagoon, trading through water-gates.
clans.hook: The Lagoon Folk know where the Drowned Choir sleeps by day.

kinds.name: Water-Gate Nobles
kinds.text: Merfolk aristocracy of the outer lagoon.

kinds.name: Sea-Elves
kinds.text: Elves who live beneath the water.

kinds.name: Coral-Weavers
kinds.text: Grow coral into jewellery and buildings.

profile.origin: The Lagoon Folk are the merfolk and sea-elves of Lirian's outer lagoon, who were living in the old city before it drowned. When the sea rose, they stayed; the humans built the new city on top.
profile.society: A water-court under a queen, with noble houses, trident guards and coral-weaver guilds. They trade with the city through carved water-gates.
profile.beliefs: The sea keeps what it is given; the old city is a grave, and graves are not for sirens.
profile.relations: Trading partners of the doge, rivals of the Canal Otters for diving rights, enemies of the Drowned Choir.
profile.war: Trident Guard fight in currents; sea-elf mages call the tide.
profile.trade: Pearls, coral jewellery, sea-silk and secrets of the drowned city.
npcs: Knows where the Drowned Choir sleeps by day.
Thinks the city should be left to the sirens.
A young merfolk artist who sneaks into the canals to sell her work.
profile.strengths: Water combat, tide-magic, knowledge of the drowned city.
quests: Lead a raid on the Drowned Belltowers by day with Corallin's guard.
Expose Nerith's dealings with the sirens.
profile.gameplay: Underwater sections in Lirian; water-gate fast travel.

clans.name: The Lanternwings
clans.look: Moth-folk with pale wings and huge dark eyes, drawn to light.
clans.culture: They gather the moon-glass by night and are the first to lose their light to Ilyanthe.
clans.hook: A Lanternwing has flown toward the red moon and not come back.

kinds.name: Glass-Gatherers
kinds.text: Moth-folk who collect moon-glass by night.

kinds.name: Lightless
kinds.text: Moth-folk whose light Ilyanthe has taken.

profile.origin: The Lanternwings are moth-folk who appeared on the Lustrine Shores the same year as the moon-glass, drawn by its light. They have gathered it by night ever since.
profile.society: Night-flocks of gatherers led by pale-winged elders; dust-seers read the future in the patterns their wings leave.
profile.beliefs: Light is to be gathered and given away, never hoarded. The red moon is a hungry light.
profile.relations: Partners of the glass-gatherers' guild; the first to lose their light to Ilyanthe.
profile.war: Blinding wing-dust and swarming.
profile.trade: Moon-glass gathering and lamp-making.
npcs: Has watched three of her flock lose their light.
Read the red moon's dust and has not slept since.
Flew toward the red moon and did not come back.
profile.weaknesses: Drawn to bright light; fragile wings.
quests: Find out what happened to Flit.
Help Ennis interpret the red moon's dust.
profile.gameplay: Night-gathering of moon-glass; Lanternwing lamps are light sources that never run out.

clans.name: The Hundred-Stair Monks
clans.leader: Abbot Wen Jinghai of the Still Flame
clans.look: Monks in robes and bandages, martial artists of fire and staff.
clans.culture: The martial monks of Shen-Lu's sects, split into orders devoted to fire, stillness and the staff, who settle doctrine by duel.
clans.hook: A monk has broken her vow of stillness to fight the Colossus.

profile.origin: The Hundred-Stair Monks were a single school before the Hundred-Stair Schism split it into rival sects. Each order still claims to be the true heir of the founder.
profile.society: Four orders (Still Flame, Iron Staff, Silent Stair and Wandering Fists), each under an abbot, with disciples ranked by the stairs they have climbed.
profile.beliefs: Cultivation of qi leads to oneness with the mountain. Pride is the poison that split the school.
profile.relations: Rivals of each other and of the Vanari; allies against the Hunger Colossus, reluctantly.
profile.war: Fire-palms, staff forms, silent strikes and wandering fist styles.
profile.trade: Training, manuals and medicine.
npcs: Abbot Wen Jinghai of the Still Flame
Believes the Colossus can be fought without qi.
Sister Mei of the Silent Stair
Has broken her vow of silence to warn of the Colossus.
Travels the crossroads challenging every master.
quests: Reunite the four orders against the Colossus.
Find out which sect built the Colossus.
profile.gameplay: Martial-arts class trainers in Shen-Lu; order choice affects available techniques.

clans.name: The Undercity Whiskers
clans.look: Rat-folk in scavenged armour, alchemists with green fire, swashbucklers.
clans.culture: Rat-folk of Cinderhole's lowest tunnels, smugglers and mask-makers.
clans.hook: A rat-folk mask-maker can make a mask that filters Vasque's smoke.

kinds.name: Tunnel-Runners
kinds.text: Know every tunnel under the crater.

profile.origin: The Undercity Whiskers are rat-folk who came to Cinderhole with the first miners, living in the walls of the mine. When the seams caught fire and the humans fled, the Whiskers stayed and learned to breathe the smoke.
profile.society: Gangs and guilds in the lowest tunnels: mask-makers, green-fire alchemists, tunnel-runners and rapier-swinging swashbucklers. Gang bosses answer to the mask-makers, because without masks no one breathes.
profile.beliefs: Air is life and a good mask is a good friend. Everyone in Cinderhole owes a rat a favour, whether they know it or not.
profile.relations: Smugglers for every gang, rivals of the Velvet Knives, enemies of Vasque when he closes the chimneys.
profile.war: Rapiers, alchemical bombs, smoke-bombs and ambushes in tunnels too small for anyone else.
profile.trade: Smoke-masks, alchemy, smuggling and tunnel-guiding.
npcs: Can make a mask that filters even Vasque's magic smoke.
Makes bombs that are mostly safe and potions that are mostly not.
Fancies himself a hero, and occasionally is one.
profile.strengths: Stealth, alchemy, tunnels, resistance to smoke.
profile.weaknesses: Small; distrusted by everyone above ground.
quests: Help Skritch make the smoke-mask that could free Cinderhole from Vasque.
Smuggle a refugee family out through the tunnels.
profile.gameplay: Smoke-mask crafting is required for Cinderhole's choked districts; rat tunnels provide shortcuts.

clans.name: The Capfolk
clans.look: Walking mushrooms of every size, from tiny sprouts to towering bruisers.
clans.culture: Mushroom-folk who live alongside the Thimblefolk and the beetles; Mycelia is their nightmare cousin.
clans.hook: A Capfolk elder says the Spore Lord was once one of them.

kinds.name: Morel Mystics
kinds.text: Mushroom-folk who speak with the soil.

profile.origin: The Capfolk are walking mushrooms who sprouted in Mossdeep's warm, mana-rich soil. They say they grew from the same root-web as Mycelia, long ago, before the Spore Lord went wrong.
profile.society: Rings of mushrooms that grow from one spore-mother. The oldest Puffballs speak for each ring, and new Sprouts appear after every warm rain.
profile.beliefs: Everything rots and everything returns; the soil remembers. To spread without asking is the worst crime a fungus can commit.
profile.relations: Gentle neighbours of the Thimblefolk, allies of the Carapace, and horrified by Mycelia, whom they call the Cousin.
profile.war: Toadstool Guards fight with staves; Morel Mystics release sleeping-spores that never harm.
profile.trade: Medicinal mushrooms, soil-reading and composting for the Thimblefolk gardens.
npcs: Says the Spore Lord was once one of them and knows its true name.
Can hear the root-web, and the Cousin's voice in it.
Newly grown and asking everyone what it is for.
quests: Learn Mycelia's true name from Old Puffball and carry it to Sylvaran.
Help Inky Cap listen to the root-web without being taken by it.
profile.gameplay: The Capfolk link Mossdeep to the Sylvaran blight questline; spore-crafting recipes.

clans.name: The Inkwardens
clans.look: Octopus-folk with tentacled lower bodies, tridents and ink.
clans.culture: Deep sea-folk of the Hollow Sea, keepers of the deepest charts.
clans.hook: An Inkwarden has charted the Lumen-Eater's hunting grounds.

profile.origin: The Inkwardens are octopus-folk of the Hollow Sea who were there before the boat-towns arrived. They charted the lightless ocean by touch and taste, and their charts are the best in the world below.
profile.society: Solitary scholars who gather only to share charts. Chartmasters hold the deepest maps; Ink-Mages and Trident Lords protect them.
profile.beliefs: Knowledge is a current; hoard it and it stagnates. Every chart must be copied before its maker dies.
profile.relations: Chart-sellers to the boat-towns, allies of the Drifting, hunted by the Lumen-Eater.
profile.war: Ink clouds, constriction, tridents and camouflage.
profile.trade: Charts of the Hollow Sea, pearls and deep-salvage.
npcs: Has charted the Lumen-Eater's hunting grounds.
Writes spells in ink that glow in the dark.
Lost three arms to the Lumen-Eater and grew them back angrier.
quests: Use Octavian's chart to plan an ambush on the Lumen-Eater.
Copy a dying Chartmaster's maps before they are lost.
profile.gameplay: Chart-buying reveals the Hollow Sea map; Inkwarden allies blind enemies with ink.

clans.name: The Hill-Orcs
clans.look: Orcs of every temperament: shamans, warriors, a red-bearded elder.
clans.culture: Wild orc clans of Moraveil's northern hills; some follow Grakkus, some fear him.
clans.hook: An orc shaman wants to warn the truce council, and needs an escort to reach it alive.

kinds.name: Hill-Herders
kinds.text: Orcs who herd goats and avoid war.

kinds.name: Truce-Seekers
kinds.text: Orcs who want to join the Moraveil truce.

profile.origin: The Hill-Orcs are the wild orc clans of Moraveil's northern hills, herders and raiders since before the kingdom. Some have followed Grakkus; others fear what he will make of them.
profile.society: Clans led by red-bearded shamans in peace and war-chiefs in war; herders, warriors and diplomats each have their place.
profile.beliefs: The spirits of the hills speak through fire and smoke. Strength serves the clan, not the self.
profile.relations: Divided: Axe-Brothers follow Grakkus, Truce-Seekers want to join Moraveil's council, herders want to be left alone.
profile.war: Axe-Brothers in heavy furs; shamans with fire-spirits.
profile.trade: Goats, wool, furs and hill-herbs.
npcs: Wants to warn the truce council about Grakkus.
Wants to sell her goats in the Moraveil market.
quests: Escort Urzha to the truce council alive.
Persuade Grosh to abandon Grakkus.
profile.gameplay: Turning Hill-Orc clans weakens Grakkus's siege; a possible future member of the truce.

clans.name: The Orca Lords
clans.look: Orca-folk, black and white, huge and powerful.
clans.culture: Sea-hunters who share the fishing grounds with the villages and fear the Ice-Jaw.
clans.hook: The Orca Lords will hunt Ysgrath if the villages lend them their best harpoons.

kinds.name: Floe-Breakers
kinds.text: Orca-folk who break the ice to hunt.

kinds.name: Song-Callers
kinds.text: Call the pod together across the sea.

profile.origin: The Orca Lords are orca-folk who have hunted Whitewater Reach's waters for longer than the villages have stood. The first fishers made a pact with them: the orcas would drive fish to the ice-holes, and the villagers would share the catch.
profile.society: Pods led by Pod-Kings and their mothers; Song-Callers keep the pod together across miles of sea; young bulls prove themselves by breaking floes.
profile.beliefs: The sea feeds those who share it. A broken pact is a hole in the ice that never freezes.
profile.relations: Pact-partners of the fishing villages, allies of the Floe-Knights and the Iceclaws, hunted by Ysgrath.
profile.war: Floe-breaking charges, coordinated pod hunts and wave-attacks that wash enemies off the ice.
profile.trade: Fish-driving, ice-breaking and deep-water escort.
npcs: Will hunt Ysgrath if the villages lend them their best harpoons.
Can call the pod from across the Reach, and has heard Ysgrath singing back.
Eager to prove himself by breaking the Broken Floe.
quests: Broker the harpoon pact between Orvald and the villages.
Find out why Ysgrath sings back to Siv.
profile.gameplay: Orca allies in the Ysgrath fight; pod-calling summons for water combat.

clans.name: The Canal Otters
clans.look: Otter-folk gondoliers, archers and gentlemen.
clans.culture: Lirian's gondoliers and divers, cheerful and nosy.
clans.hook: A canal otter has heard the Drowned Choir and wants to follow it, with someone holding the rope.

kinds.name: Canal Divers
kinds.text: Dive for the coins thrown into the canals.

kinds.name: Otter Archers
kinds.text: Defend the canals from the Drowned Choir.

profile.origin: The Canal Otters came to Lirian with the first fishing boats and never left. When the city grew, they became its gondoliers, divers and gossips, and today no deal in Lirian is secret from them for long.
profile.society: Family rafts led by the eldest gondolier; the divers' guild and the gondoliers' guild argue about everything except the city's safety.
profile.beliefs: Water is home and the canals are family. Every coin in the canal is a prayer, and divers return a tenth of what they find to the water.
profile.relations: Friends of everyone, rivals of the Lagoon Folk for the best diving spots, quietly paid informants of the doge.
profile.war: Otter Archers shoot from gondolas; divers drag attackers under.
profile.trade: Gondola fares, diving, gossip and the occasional smuggled letter.
npcs: Has heard the Drowned Choir and wants to follow it, with someone holding the rope.
Runs the finest fish restaurant in Lirian and knows every secret spoken at its tables.
The youngest diver in the guild and the best at finding lost rings.
quests: Hold Pip's rope while he follows the Drowned Choir's song.
Use Madame Whiskerton's gossip to find out who in the doge's council deals with the sirens.
profile.gameplay: Gondola fast travel in Lirian; otter informants sell rumours.

clans.name: The Stillhorns
clans.look: Minotaur and ox-folk, heavy-horned and patient.
clans.culture: Herders and tremor-readers of the Quaking Lands, who feel quakes through their hooves.
clans.hook: A Stillhorn elder has felt something in the ground that is not Quakeback.

kinds.name: Tremor-Readers
kinds.text: Read the ground through their hooves.

kinds.name: Deep-Hooves
kinds.text: Ancient minotaurs who remember the old maps.

profile.origin: The Stillhorns are minotaur and ox-folk who herd the Quaking Lands' stone-horned cattle. They were reading tremors through their hooves long before the human Stillers learned to.
profile.society: Herds led by Deep-Hooves elders; tremor-readers and guards serve the spring-towns as well as their own herds.
profile.beliefs: The ground speaks to those who listen with their feet. Quakeback is not a monster but a sleeper with bad dreams.
profile.relations: Partners of the Stiller spring-towns, uneasy about anyone who wants to fight Quakeback.
profile.war: Minotaur Guards with great axes; charge attacks that knock enemies down.
profile.trade: Cattle, tremor-charts, leather and crystals brought up by quakes.
npcs: Has felt something in the ground that is not Quakeback.
Young and talented; the elders doubt him.
Knows every cow by name and every quake by smell.
quests: Find what Tauron felt under the ground.
Prove Asterion's prediction of a great quake right.
profile.gameplay: Tremor-warning system in the Quaking Lands; Stillhorn allies stabilise ground during fights.

clans.name: The Scholar Owls
clans.look: Owl-folk scholars and sentinels with feathered robes.
clans.culture: The examination-masters of Haneul, who see in the dark and remember everything.
clans.hook: A Scholar Owl has failed a candidate who might have saved the wall.

kinds.name: Examiners
kinds.text: Set and judge the great examinations.

kinds.name: Quill-Keepers
kinds.text: Keep the records of the kingdom.

kinds.name: Feather-Mages
kinds.text: Owl-folk who cast spells with feathers.

profile.origin: The Scholar Owls were Haneul's first examiners, owl-folk scholars who invented the great examinations so that the kingdom would be ruled by learning rather than birth.
profile.society: Examiners, archivists, night-sentinels and feather-mages, ranked by the examinations they have passed and set.
profile.beliefs: Learning is the only true nobility. A question asked well is half answered.
profile.relations: Advisers to the king, rivals of the Tigerguard for influence, respected by every scholar in the world.
profile.war: Night-Sentinels watch the wall in the dark; feather-mages cast spells written on their own feathers.
profile.trade: Education, examination, archives and scholarship.
npcs: Failed a candidate who might have saved the wall.
Keeps the records of every examination since the first.
Has seen something on the red gate at night.
quests: Find the failed candidate and give them a second chance.
Help Haneulbit observe the red gate at night.
profile.gameplay: Examination questline unlocks magic schools in Haneul.

clans.name: The Brew-Bears
clans.look: Panda-folk brewers, monks and martial artists.
clans.culture: Shen-Lu's brewers and wandering fighters, beloved at every crossroads.
clans.hook: A Brew-Bear's spirit wine might restore drained qi, if someone can fetch the herbs.

kinds.name: Wandering Pandas
kinds.text: Travel the crossroads, seeking good tea.

profile.origin: The Brew-Bears are panda-folk who came to Shen-Lu as wandering brewers, found the mountain water perfect for spirit wine and never left. Every sect owes them a debt, usually unpaid.
profile.society: Brewing families who wander between towns, settling for a season wherever the water is good. Master Brewers lead; Drunken Fists protect; Bamboo Wardens tend the groves.
profile.beliefs: A good drink makes peace and a good fight makes friends. Never brew in anger; the wine remembers.
profile.relations: Friends of every sect, especially the Vanari; welcome at every crossroads inn; enemies of no one except bad tea.
profile.war: Drunken-fist martial arts that look like stumbling until they land; staff-work with bamboo poles.
profile.trade: Spirit wine, tea, medicinal brews and bamboo.
npcs: Believes his spirit wine might restore drained qi.
Guards the bamboo forests from the Colossus's drain.
Always looking for good tea; finds trouble instead.
quests: Fetch the herbs for Bao's qi-restoring wine from a grey peak.
Help Yuyu defend the bamboo forest from the Colossus.
profile.gameplay: Spirit-wine brewing restores qi in Shen-Lu; a drunken-fist mentor.

clans.name: The Plateback
clans.look: Pangolin-folk with overlapping scales, curling into balls for defence.
clans.culture: Riders of Thalassa who patch her hide and polish her barnacles.
clans.hook: A Plateback has found a wound on Thalassa's back that goes very deep.

kinds.name: Curl-Guards
kinds.text: Curl into armoured balls to defend.

kinds.name: Sand-Diggers
kinds.text: Dig out the barnacles and the parasites.

profile.origin: The Plateback are pangolin-folk born on Thalassa's back who have tended her hide for as long as the town has ridden her. They say she was carrying them before she carried anyone else.
profile.society: Hide-crews led by Hide-Wardens; each crew is responsible for a patch of Thalassa's back and is named after it.
profile.beliefs: Thalassa is mother and home; a wound in her hide is a wound in every Plateback.
profile.relations: Partners of the Whale-Singers, wary of the sand pirates, terrified of Glassmaw.
profile.war: Curl-Guards roll into armoured balls and bowl through enemies; Sand-Diggers ambush from beneath the sand.
profile.trade: Hide-care, barnacle-cleaning, shed scales sold as armour.
npcs: Has found a wound on Thalassa's back that goes very deep.
The best bowler on the whale and very proud of it.
Sells shed scales to every visitor and swears each one is lucky.
quests: Find out what made the deep wound in Thalassa's back.
Help Rolla defend the town from sand pirates.
profile.gameplay: Pangolin scale armour sets; hide-care minigame to keep Thalassa healthy.

clans.name: The Velvet Knives
clans.look: Panther-folk assassins and thieves in black.
clans.culture: Cinderhole's quietest guild, who sell secrets to Vasque and his enemies alike.
clans.hook: A Velvet Knife has been hired to kill the alchemist who could put out the fires.

profile.origin: The Velvet Knives began as a guild of panther-folk thieves who learned to breathe Cinderhole's smoke when no one else could. They now sell secrets to Vasque and to his enemies alike.
profile.society: A matriarchal guild under the Velvet Mother, with silent assassins, whisperer spies and shadow-dancer thieves.
profile.beliefs: Every secret has a price; every price has a buyer. Never kill a child; never break a contract.
profile.relations: Vasque's informants and his greatest danger; rivals of the Undercity Whiskers.
profile.war: Silent blades, poison and smoke.
profile.trade: Secrets, theft and assassination.
npcs: Has accepted a contract to kill the alchemist who could put out the fires.
Has started to doubt the contract.
quests: Protect the alchemist from the Velvet Knives.
Turn Shade-Paw.
profile.gameplay: Stealth faction in Cinderhole; spy network.

clans.name: The Floe-Knights
clans.leader: Sir Pengrove of the White Shield
clans.look: Penguin-folk knights with round shields and ice spears.
clans.culture: Defenders of the ice villages, formal and fearless.
clans.hook: The Floe-Knights have challenged Ysgrath to single combat.

kinds.name: White Shields
kinds.text: Penguin knights with round ice shields.

profile.origin: The Floe-Knights are penguin-folk who defended the ice villages from the frost serpents generations ago and were knighted by the villagers for it. They have kept the ice ever since.
profile.society: An order of knights led by its eldest member, with Emperor Guards, spear-carriers and slide-scouts. Knights are chosen by the villagers, not the order.
profile.beliefs: Honour is earned on the ice. A knight who abandons a village is no knight.
profile.relations: Defenders of the ice villages, allies of the Orca Lords and the Iceclaws, sworn enemies of Ysgrath.
profile.war: Round ice shields, ice-spears and belly-slide charges across the floes.
profile.trade: Protection, fishing and ice-craft.
npcs: Sir Pengrove of the White Shield
Has challenged Ysgrath to single combat.
The largest knight in the order, and the gentlest.
The fastest scout across the ice.
profile.weaknesses: Slow on land; outmatched by Ysgrath alone.
quests: Talk Sir Pengrove out of single combat, or help him prepare.
Scout the Broken Floe with Skid.
profile.gameplay: Ice-combat training; Floe-Knight allies hold the line during the Ysgrath siege.

clans.name: The Free Captains
clans.look: Pirates of every kind: swashbucklers, quartermasters, gunners.
clans.culture: Goldmere's elected captains and their crews.
clans.hook: A Free Captain wants a truce with the port to fight the Krakenmother.

kinds.name: Quartermasters
kinds.text: Keep the loot fair and the crew fed.

kinds.name: Powder-Monkeys
kinds.text: Young crew who carry the powder.

profile.origin: The Free Captains are Goldmere's pirate crews, many of them refugees, deserters and runaways who chose the sea over the law. They elect their captains and remove them by vote.
profile.society: Crews under elected captains, with quartermasters, gunners and powder-monkeys; captains meet in a council on the largest stilt-town.
profile.beliefs: Freedom first, loot second. A crew that cannot vote out its captain is not free.
profile.relations: Rivals and trading partners of Port Goldmere; enemies of the Krakenmother; employers of the Reef-Sharks.
profile.war: Cannon, cutlass and boarding.
profile.trade: Plunder, smuggling, rum.
npcs: Wants a truce with the port to fight the Krakenmother.
Keeps the loot fair and the crew honest.
A runaway who dreams of being captain.
quests: Broker Anne's truce with the port.
Help Patch earn a vote.
profile.gameplay: Pirate faction in Goldmere; ship-to-ship combat events.

clans.name: The Iceclaws
clans.look: Polar-bear-folk shamans and warriors with lightning in their fists.
clans.culture: Shamans and hunters of the ice, who call storms against the leviathan.
clans.hook: An Iceclaw shaman is losing her storms.

kinds.name: White Hunters
kinds.text: Hunt seals and walrus on the floes.

kinds.name: Rune-Bears
kinds.text: Polar bears who carve runes in ice.

profile.origin: The Iceclaws are polar-bear shamans and hunters who learned to call storms from the auroras over Whitewater Reach. They have hunted the floes alongside the villages since the first ice-fishing hole was cut.
profile.society: Dens led by Ice-Mothers; storm-shamans are chosen by the auroras, which are said to flicker over a cub's den when it is born with the gift.
profile.beliefs: Storms are the sky's breath; a shaman borrows them and must give them back.
profile.relations: Allies of the Floe-Knights and the Orca Lords; Ysgrath's cold is stealing their storms.
profile.war: Lightning called down on the ice, claws and rune-carved spears.
profile.trade: Furs, ivory, storm-warnings and rune-carved charms.
npcs: Keeps the dens and the old aurora-songs.
profile.weaknesses: Heat; the Ice-Jaw's cold drains their power.
quests: Find out what is stealing Ulluq's storms.
Hunt with Nanuq on the floes.
profile.gameplay: Storm-calling abilities; aurora events boost lightning magic in Whitewater Reach.

clans.name: The Plague-Beaks
clans.look: Crow-folk in plague-doctor masks and long coats.
clans.culture: Battlefield healers and grave-keepers who follow every army.
clans.hook: A Plague-Beak has noticed that the Choir's dead do not rot.

kinds.name: Beak Doctors
kinds.text: Plague-doctor crows who heal the wounded.

kinds.name: Grave-Keepers
kinds.text: Bury the dead of every army.

kinds.name: Crow-Scouts
kinds.text: Follow armies and report their movements.

kinds.name: Raven-Mages
kinds.text: Crows who speak with the dead.

profile.origin: The Plague-Beaks are crow-folk who have followed armies since the first war, tending the wounded and burying the dead. They wear beaked masks filled with herbs to keep the sickness of battlefields away.
profile.society: A loose order of doctors, grave-keepers, scouts and raven-mages, sworn to treat all sides equally.
profile.beliefs: Death is a doorway; a good doctor stands beside it and asks it to wait.
profile.relations: Welcome on every battlefield and trusted by no army; now deeply afraid of the Choir of Chains.
profile.war: They avoid fighting, but raven-mages can command the dead to lie still.
profile.trade: Healing, burial, medicine and information on troop movements.
npcs: Has noticed the Choir's dead do not rot.
Buries the dead of every side with the same care.
Watches every army in the Marches.
profile.weaknesses: Neutrality makes enemies on all sides.
quests: Investigate why the Choir's dead do not rot.
Help Sister Rookwyn bury the dead at the Field of Coins.
profile.gameplay: Healers who revive companions on battlefields; Plague-Beak research reveals the Choir's weakness.

clans.name: The Ember-tails
clans.look: Red-panda-folk adventurers, archers and street kids.
clans.culture: Cheerful wanderers of the bamboo villages.
clans.hook: An Ember-tail kid has stolen one of Kurogane's masks.

kinds.name: Street-Captains
kinds.text: Leaders of the red-panda street gangs.

kinds.name: Bamboo Archers
kinds.text: Red-panda archers of the bamboo villages.

kinds.name: Lantern-Thieves
kinds.text: Steal lanterns from the spirit festivals.

profile.origin: The Ember-tails are red-panda-folk of Hoshizora's bamboo villages, cheerful wanderers who arrived generations ago with tea carts and stayed for the festivals.
profile.society: Loose bands led by street-captains, often young; elders run tea stalls and tell stories.
profile.beliefs: Every festival is a chance to steal a lantern and give it back with a better candle.
profile.relations: Beloved by villagers, annoying to samurai, an unexpected thorn in Kurogane's side.
profile.war: Bamboo bows and quick hands.
profile.trade: Tea, carved bamboo and stolen-then-returned lanterns.
npcs: Has stolen one of Kurogane's masks.
Knows every rumour in the bamboo sea.
The best shot in the villages.
quests: Protect Kip from Kurogane's hunters and study the stolen mask.
Help Granny Hoshi set up a festival stall during the siege.
profile.gameplay: Street-urchin informants in Hoshizora; mask-theft questline reveals how Kurogane's masks work.

clans.name: The Hornwall
clans.look: Rhino-folk masons and brawlers, heavily armoured.
clans.culture: Bastion's master masons, who build the new rings.
clans.hook: A Hornwall mason has found sabotage in the foundations.

kinds.name: Stone-Haulers
kinds.text: Carry the stone for the walls.

profile.origin: The Hornwall are rhino-folk masons who came to Bastion when its second ring was raised, hired for a season. They stayed, and they have built every ring since.
profile.society: Mason-crews led by Master Masons; haulers carry the stone, rammers clear the breaches and Iron-Horns hold them. A Hornwall's horn is notched for every ring they have helped raise.
profile.beliefs: A wall is only as strong as its foundation, and a people only as strong as its builders. A stone from the broken ring goes into every new one.
profile.relations: Inseparable from the Shieldwall, honoured by the Warden, and the first target of Thrakka's saboteurs.
profile.war: Rammers charge through enemy lines; Iron-Horns hold a breach alone with shields of fitted stone.
profile.trade: Masonry, quarrying, siegeworks and stone sold to the south.
npcs: Has found sabotage in the new ring's foundations.
Can carry a stone the size of a cart up a ladder.
Held a breach alone for an hour during the last siege.
quests: Find the saboteur in the masons' crews before the next charge.
Hold a breach with Dace during the next horde attack.
profile.gameplay: Wall-building and repair during Bastion sieges; breach-defence encounters.

clans.name: The Iron Legions
clans.look: Roman-style legionaries in segmented armour with red cloaks.
clans.culture: Vharlen's legions, drilled from childhood, who carry their founders' pledge into every battle and bury their standards with their dead.
clans.hook: A legion has lost its standard to Morvane.

profile.origin: The Iron Legions were founded with the empire itself, when the first emperor swore every citizen to serve and carved the pledge beneath the barracks. They have held the demon frontier for generations.
profile.society: Legions of legionaries under centurions and legates; Praetorians guard the emperor; auxiliaries scout the passes. Every citizen serves a term, and rank in the legion shapes rank at home.
profile.beliefs: The pledge first, the empire second, the self last. A legion that loses its standard is disbanded in shame.
profile.relations: The empire's sword and shield; wary of the guild; respectful of Morvane as an enemy.
profile.war: Shield walls, short swords, javelins and disciplined manoeuvre; auxiliaries skirmish in the passes.
profile.trade: Military service; the legions consume half the empire's grain and iron.
npcs: Lost a standard to Morvane and means to take it back.
Twenty years on the frontier and still alive.
Knows every pass and every shortcut.
quests: Recover the lost standard from Morvane's camp.
Scout a fallen fort with Lucan.
profile.gameplay: Legion reputation track in Vharlen; standard-recovery questline.

clans.name: The Pipers
clans.look: Satyrs and fauns with goat legs, pipes and spears.
clans.culture: Musicians and messengers of both courts, who are allowed to cross between them.
clans.hook: A Piper has been forbidden from playing, and the forest is going quiet.

profile.origin: The Pipers are satyrs and fauns who wandered into Everdusk playing music so beautiful that both courts claimed them. They are the only folk allowed to cross freely between the Summer and Winter Courts.
profile.society: Loose bands of musicians, messengers and wild fauns; each Piper's tune is their passport.
profile.beliefs: Music is older than the courts; a forest without song is a dead forest.
profile.relations: Messengers for both courts, friends of the Antlered Court, now forbidden to play by the Briar King.
profile.war: Spears and enchanting tunes that make enemies dance until they drop.
profile.trade: Music, messages and fey-goods.
npcs: Has been forbidden to play, and the forest is going quiet.
Plays for both courts and spies for neither.
Lives in the deep woods and knows the forest's oldest songs.
quests: Lift the Briar King's ban on Fennick's music.
Carry a message between the courts with Melisande.
profile.gameplay: Music-based puzzles; Pipers open paths between the courts.

clans.name: The Sand-Stingers
clans.look: Scorpion-bodied folk with human torsos.
clans.culture: Nomads of the deep desert who guard the Colossus's path.
clans.hook: The Sand-Stingers want the Colossus stopped without being destroyed.

kinds.name: Dune-Claws
kinds.text: Scorpion warriors of the deep desert.

kinds.name: Burrowers
kinds.text: Hide in the sand and wait.

profile.origin: The Sand-Stingers are scorpion-bodied nomads of Sunscar's deep desert who were the vanished empire's border guards. When the empire fell, they kept guarding the borders of a land that no longer existed.
profile.society: Matriarchal clans under venom-priestesses; warriors, path-guards and burrowers serve the clan.
profile.beliefs: The sacred venom carries the clan's memory; a sting given in anger is a sin.
profile.relations: Guardians of the Colossus's path; wary of the Well-Keepers; enemies of treasure-hunters.
profile.war: Pincers, stingers and ambushes from beneath the sand.
profile.trade: Venom for medicine, desert guiding and border tolls.
npcs: Wants the Colossus stopped without being destroyed.
Keeps the clan's memory in the sacred venom.
Has fought the Colossus and lived.
quests: Find a way to stop the Colossus without destroying it.
Learn the clan's memory through Sethra's venom ritual.
profile.gameplay: Sand-Stinger antivenom crafting; allies in the Colossus fight.

clans.name: The Selkies
clans.look: Seal-folk who can shed their skins.
clans.culture: Fjord-folk who trade with the longhouses and marry into them.
clans.hook: A selkie's skin has been stolen by a jarl's son.

kinds.name: Skinless
kinds.text: Selkies whose skins have been stolen.

profile.origin: The Selkies are seal-folk of Frostveil's fjords who can shed their skins and walk on land. They have traded and married with the longhouse clans for generations, and half of Skjaldheim has a selkie grandmother.
profile.society: Families led by skin-keepers, who guard the shed skins of those living ashore. A selkie on land without their skin cannot return to the sea.
profile.beliefs: A selkie's skin is their soul. To steal it is the worst crime, and to give it freely is the deepest love.
profile.relations: Kin to the human clans through marriage; friends of the Ursa and the Hill-Kings; wary of jarls' sons.
profile.war: Rarely fight; when they do, they drag enemies into the icy water.
profile.trade: Fish, seal-oil, songs and the finest fjord-pearls.
npcs: Her daughter's skin has been stolen by a jarl's son.
Sings to the longhouses on winter nights; every song is a true story.
Guards his family's skins in a sea-cave no one else can find.
quests: Recover Ronnagh's daughter's skin without starting a feud with the jarl.
Hear all of Moira's songs and learn the one about the summer that lasted a hundred years.
profile.gameplay: A selkie skin-cloak allows underwater exploration in Frostveil.

clans.name: The Hollow Ones
clans.look: Living shadows and silhouettes with long limbs.
clans.culture: Shadow-folk of the deepest webs, who never come into the light.
clans.hook: A Hollow One has started casting a shadow of its own.

kinds.name: Long-Limbs
kinds.text: Stretched shadows that hunt in the dark.

kinds.name: Casting
kinds.text: Shadows that have begun to cast shadows.

profile.origin: The Hollow Ones are living shadows from the deepest webs below Umbravel, older than the city. They were there in the dark when the founders arrived, and they let the founders stay.
profile.society: No leaders in the usual sense; the oldest, the Unshadowed, are listened to. They gather in silence and communicate by touch.
profile.beliefs: Light is a visitor; darkness is home. To cast a shadow is to become something other than what you were.
profile.relations: Careful allies of the Nightwings; the Web Queen's brood avoids them; the city treats them as ghosts.
profile.war: They smother light and strike from the dark with long, stretching limbs.
profile.trade: Darkness itself: they can make places unseen, and the weaver-guilds pay for hidden vaults.
npcs: The oldest shadow; knows what lived in the cavern before the city.
Stretches across whole districts to hunt the Web Queen's brood.
Has started casting a shadow of its own and is frightened.
profile.strengths: Stealth, darkness, immunity to physical harm in shadow.
quests: Find out why Flicker-Without-Light has begun to cast a shadow.
Ask the Unshadowed what lived in the cavern before Umbravel.
profile.gameplay: Shadow-step abilities in Umbravel; Hollow Ones hide the player from patrols.

clans.name: The Reef-Sharks
clans.look: Shark-folk, from naval officers to gaping monsters.
clans.culture: Hunters and enforcers of the reefs, hired by both port and pirates.
clans.hook: The Reef-Sharks have stopped hunting near the wreck-tide; they are afraid.

profile.origin: The Reef-Sharks are shark-folk who hunted Goldmere's reefs before the port was built. When the salvagers came, the sharks found that enforcing claims paid better than hunting fish.
profile.society: Commodores lead squadrons of Grinwaters, Hammerheads and Great Whites; rank is shown by teeth worn on a cord.
profile.beliefs: Keep moving or drown. Never bite the hand that pays you, until the contract ends.
profile.relations: Hired by both port and pirates; old rivals of the Shellguard; now too frightened of the wreck-tide to hunt there.
profile.war: Fast, brutal strikes in the water; Hammerheads scout, Great Whites finish.
profile.trade: Enforcement, protection and deep-water escort.
npcs: Has stopped hunting near the wreck-tide and won't say why.
Saw something in the deep that made him swim home.
The largest shark-folk on the coast, retired and bored.
profile.strengths: Speed and power in water, smell for blood.
profile.weaknesses: Must keep moving; poor on land.
quests: Find out what frightened the Reef-Sharks away from the wreck-tide.
Hire Big Grey out of retirement for one last job.
profile.gameplay: Hireable underwater escorts in Goldmere; their fear is an early warning of the Krakenmother.

clans.name: The Coilborn
clans.look: Naga-like serpent-folk with swords and spears.
clans.culture: Guardians of the garden springs, old allies of the divs.
clans.hook: A Coilborn guardian knows where the original treaty is carved.

profile.origin: The Coilborn are serpent-folk who guarded Zarvan's springs for the div-kings before people came. When the garden treaties were signed in water, they were the witnesses.
profile.society: Spring-clans led by Wardens; naga priestesses keep the treaties; cobra guards defend the springs; sand-coils scout the desert edge.
profile.beliefs: A treaty witnessed is a treaty bound. Water forgets, but serpents don't.
profile.relations: Allies of the Sun-Hawks; servants of the shah and remembered friends of Zahhar; caught between.
profile.war: Curved swords, hooded charges and venom.
profile.trade: Spring-guarding, treaty-witnessing, venom for medicine.
npcs: Knows where the original treaty is carved.
Can recite every garden treaty, word for word.
Has defected to Zahhar's side and believes he is right.
quests: Follow Nagasha to the carved treaty in the Div Springs.
Bring Kaal back, or hear why he left.
profile.gameplay: Treaty-recital dialogue unlocks the peaceful resolution with Zahhar.

clans.name: The Shellmoot
clans.look: Snail-folk, slow and wise, in moss-grown shells.
clans.culture: Greymoor's oldest folk, who remember the abbey on dry ground.
clans.hook: A Shellmoot elder remembers what the abbey was built to hold down.

kinds.name: Spiral Elders
kinds.text: Ancient snails who remember the abbey.

kinds.name: Shell-Sleepers
kinds.text: Snails who rarely leave their shells.

profile.origin: The Shellmoot are snail-folk who have lived in Greymoor since it was a lake of clear water. The oldest remember the abbey on dry ground and the causeway that led to it.
profile.society: Slow moots of elders that take years to decide anything. Slime-Trackers lay trails through the fen; Moss-Shells tend the reed beds; Shell-Sleepers rarely leave their shells at all.
profile.beliefs: Haste is the root of every mistake. What sinks slowly can be raised slowly.
profile.relations: Friends of the Bogkin, distant cousins of the Capfolk, wary of the Hollow Abbot, whom some of them remember as a young monk.
profile.war: They barely fight; their slime trails trap enemies and their shells turn blades.
profile.trade: Slime-medicine for burns, memory, and the safest paths through the fen.
npcs: Remembers what the abbey was built to hold down.
Covered in moss, very proud of it, and the fastest snail in the fen.
Leaves glowing trails that guide travellers through the fog.
quests: Sit with Spiraleth long enough to hear the whole story of the abbey (it takes a week).
Follow Trail's glowing path to the Peat Library.
profile.gameplay: Lore-keepers for Greymoor; Shellmoot trails serve as guided paths through the fog.

clans.name: The Slow Sages
clans.look: Sloth-folk of great patience, in robes and halos.
clans.culture: Lumbaya's canopy-dwelling sages, who keep the old star-records.
clans.hook: A Slow Sage has been watching the sky for twenty years and finally has something to say.

profile.origin: The Slow Sages are sloth-folk who live in Lumbaya's highest canopy and have kept the temple-builders' star-records since the builders vanished. They move slowly because, they say, the stars do too.
profile.society: Each sage watches one patch of sky for life; Halo-Sloths keep the rites; Wakers, the rare fast ones, carry messages down to the villages.
profile.beliefs: Patience reveals everything. The sky is a book written slowly, and the temples were built to read it.
profile.relations: Revered by the temple villages, protected by the Silverbacks, ignored by the Nightmother, who does not think they matter.
profile.war: They do not fight; Wakers can move astonishingly fast when they must.
profile.trade: Star-readings, calendars and very slow advice.
npcs: Has watched the sky for twenty years and finally has something to say.
Keeps the rites of the Sky Temples.
A rare fast sloth who carries messages down from the canopy.
quests: Wait with Bradyon until he says what he has seen.
Help Zip carry an urgent message before the nightshifters intercept it.
profile.gameplay: Astronomy puzzles reveal why the temple roofs were torn off; Sage readings unlock Lumbaya lore.

clans.name: The Ibis Scribes
clans.look: Ibis- and stork-folk scribes in robes, with staffs and scrolls.
clans.culture: Zarvan's poets and archivists, keepers of the universities.
clans.hook: An Ibis Scribe has found a poem that could end the div war.

profile.origin: The Ibis Scribes are ibis- and stork-folk who founded Zarvan's universities. Their first scribe wrote down the garden treaties when the shahs and div-kings signed them in water.
profile.society: Universities organised by school: reed-pen scribes, poet-ibises, stork messengers and crane dancers.
profile.beliefs: A word written outlives the hand. Poetry is prayer, and the best poem ends a war.
profile.relations: Scholars of the shah's court, allies of the Sun-Hawks and the Coilborn, respected by Zahhar.
profile.war: Rarely; a scribe's weapon is a well-placed argument.
profile.trade: Scholarship, copying, poetry and teaching.
npcs: Has found a poem that could end the div war.
Writes verses that make roses bloom.
quests: Help Tahut recite the poem to Zahhar.
Deliver Shirin's verses to the Rose Palace.
profile.gameplay: Poetry-recital dialogue options in Zarvan; university library hub.

clans.name: The Tigerguard
clans.look: Tiger-folk warriors and monks, striped and powerful.
clans.culture: Haneul's elite wall-guard.
clans.hook: A Tigerguard captain has been accused of treason by the Scholar Owls.

profile.origin: The Tigerguard are tiger-folk who have guarded Haneul's wall since it was built. The first Tigerguard is said to have walked out of the mountain forest on the day the first stone was laid and asked to stand on it.
profile.society: Wall-companies under captains; striped monks train the young; white tigers are rare and revered as lucky.
profile.beliefs: The wall is a promise to everyone behind it. Courage without discipline is just noise.
profile.relations: Defenders of the king, rivals of the Scholar Owls for influence, and the demons' first target on the wall.
profile.war: Halberds, claws and martial arts; white tigers lead counter-charges.
profile.trade: Military service and martial training.
npcs: Accused of treason by the Scholar Owls.
Trains young Tigerguard in the mountain style.
A rare white tiger, young and very lucky so far.
quests: Clear Baek's name before he is executed.
Train with Monk Seol in the mountain style.
profile.gameplay: Martial-arts trainers in Haneul; the treason questline exposes a demon spy.

clans.name: The Moss-Trolls
clans.look: Huge mossy trolls, some carrying boulders.
clans.culture: Trolls of the fjord forests, wary of humans and terrified of Ymgrir.
clans.hook: A Moss-Troll has come to the longhouses asking for shelter.

kinds.name: Forest Hermits
kinds.text: Trolls who live alone in the woods.

profile.origin: The Moss-Trolls are trolls of Frostveil's fjord forests who have slept under the pines since before the longhouses were built. Ymgrir's frost giants hunt them for sport, and this winter they have come down to the longhouses for the first time.
profile.society: Loose families; elders grow so mossy they become indistinguishable from boulders. Bridge-Keepers guard crossings and ask riddles; hermits live alone in the deep woods.
profile.beliefs: Stay still and the world passes you by. A riddle answered is a friendship made.
profile.relations: Protected by the Hill-Kings, wary of humans, terrified of Ymgrir.
profile.war: Boulder-throwing, crushing blows and regeneration.
profile.trade: Bridge-tolls (paid in riddles), mushrooms and moss-medicine.
npcs: Has come to the longhouses asking for shelter.
Guards a bridge and asks a riddle no one has ever answered.
Curious, lost and following the player around.
quests: Convince the longhouses to shelter Gruumsk's family.
Answer Grubb's riddle to cross the bridge.
profile.gameplay: Troll allies in the Frostveil siege; a riddle minigame.

clans.name: The Shell-Sages
clans.leader: Elder Kamejiro of the First Promise
clans.look: Turtle-folk in samurai armour and robes, slow and wise.
clans.culture: Keepers of the islands' oldest contracts.
clans.hook: A Shell-Sage remembers the broken promise that sank an island.

kinds.name: Island-Backs
kinds.text: Turtles so old they have islands on their shells.

profile.origin: The Shell-Sages are turtle-folk who witnessed the first promises between foxes and fishermen that made the Kitsune Isles. They have kept those contracts ever since, carved on the insides of their shells.
profile.society: Elders whose shells are covered in contracts; younger turtles serve as samurai or wander as kappa cousins; the most ancient carry islands on their backs.
profile.beliefs: A promise is heavier than a shell and lasts longer. The isle that sank was a promise broken.
profile.relations: Respected by the fox shrines, consulted by the spirit inns, sorrowful about the Hollow Bride.
profile.war: Shell Samurai fight in heavy armour; kappa cousins trip enemies into water.
profile.trade: Contract-keeping, witnessing and remembering.
npcs: Elder Kamejiro of the First Promise
Remembers the broken promise that sank an island.
A river-cousin owed a cucumber debt from three generations ago.
So old an island grows on his shell; he hasn't moved in a century.
profile.weaknesses: Slowness; spilled water (for the kappa cousins).
quests: Learn from Kamejiro who broke the promise and how to mend it.
Settle Kappa Gawa's cucumber debt.
profile.gameplay: Contract-witnessing unlocks spirit-inn privileges; Shell-Sage memories reveal the Hollow Bride's past.

clans.name: The Unburied Court
clans.look: Mummified kings and soldiers in gold and linen.
clans.culture: The vanished empire's dead, waiting in the Sunken Towers.
clans.hook: The Unburied Court wants the Colossus to finish its route.

kinds.name: Pharaohs-in-Waiting
kinds.text: Mummified kings waiting to rule again.

kinds.name: Tomb Guards
kinds.text: Undead soldiers of the vanished empire.

profile.origin: The Unburied Court are the vanished empire's dead, kings and soldiers mummified for an afterlife that never came because the empire burned before the rites were finished.
profile.society: A court of the dead under a pharaoh-in-waiting, served by tomb guards, embalmer priests and lesser sand-mummies.
profile.beliefs: The rites must be completed; the empire must rise again.
profile.relations: Enemies of the Well-Keepers and the Sable Guides; they want the Colossus to finish its route.
profile.war: Tomb guards with spears and curses; priests with sand-magic.
profile.trade: None; they hoard.
npcs: Wants the Colossus to finish its route.
Has guarded the same door for a thousand years.
quests: Finish the rites and lay the court to rest.
Learn from Hesy what the Colossus's route leads to.
profile.gameplay: Undead faction in Sunscar; finishing the rites is a peaceful alternative.

clans.name: The Barrow-Host
clans.look: Skeletal knights and kings in rusted crowns.
clans.culture: Ashgrave's host from the Greyhollow barrows.
clans.hook: A skeleton knight in Ashgrave's host still wears the colours of a living family.

kinds.name: Bone Soldiers
kinds.text: The marching dead of the barrows.

profile.origin: The Barrow-Host are the dead of Greyhollow: the knights and soldiers who kept the oath their lord broke and died holding the line. When the barrows opened, they rose and followed the one man who could not follow them in life.
profile.society: An army of the dead under Ashgrave, organised as they were in life: knights, wights, foot-soldiers and the ancient crowned dead from older barrows.
profile.beliefs: The oath is all that is left. The living forgot them; they will make the living remember.
profile.relations: The siege-army of Aldmere; hated and feared by the Hearthbound; some still wear the colours of living families.
profile.war: Disciplined ranks of the dead, wights who drain the living and knights in rusted plate.
profile.trade: None.
npcs: Leads the dead who kept the oath he broke.
Still wears the colours of a living family in Ashby.
An ancient king from a barrow older than Aldmere, who serves no one.
profile.weaknesses: Silver, holy magic, remembering their names.
quests: Return Sir Edwyn to his family's memory and lay him to rest.
Learn the Barrow-Crown's story before Ashgrave uses it.
profile.gameplay: Aldmere's siege faction; naming the dead weakens them and is a non-violent counter.

clans.name: The Drowned Crews
clans.look: Skeleton pirates on ghost ships.
clans.culture: Crews the wreck-tide brought home dead.
clans.hook: A Drowned Crew wants to finish its last voyage.

profile.origin: The Drowned Crews are sailors the wreck-tide brought home dead: crews of ships that sank far across the sea and drifted to Goldmere's reefs as ghosts, still aboard their ships.
profile.society: Each ship keeps its own crew, captain and rules; the crews are bound to finish their last voyage and cannot rest until they do.
profile.beliefs: A voyage must be finished; a sailor goes home or goes nowhere.
profile.relations: Haunt the pirate stilt-towns; feared by salvagers; fought by the Krakenmother, who wants their wrecks.
profile.war: Ghost cannon that never run out of shot, cutlasses and boarding parties of the dead.
profile.trade: None, though ghost captains sometimes pay in sunken gold for passage home.
npcs: Wants to finish his last voyage, to a port that may no longer exist.
Fires a cannon that never runs out of shot.
A cabin-boy ghost who wants to go home to his mother.
quests: Help Morrin finish his voyage and lay his crew to rest.
Take Little Wick home.
profile.gameplay: Ghost-ship questlines in Goldmere; finishing voyages lays crews to rest instead of fighting them.

clans.name: The Red Barons
clans.look: Vampire nobles and beasts, red-eyed and elegant.
clans.culture: Old blood-lords of the ruined castles who profit from every war.
clans.hook: A Red Baron has offered to fight the Choir of Chains, for a price.

profile.origin: The Red Barons are vampire nobles who took the Strife Marches' ruined castles generations ago, when the wars left them empty. Every war since has fed them, and they have quietly made sure the wars never end.
profile.society: Blood-lords rule from their castles with thralls, duellists and the night-beasts that some barons become when hunger wins.
profile.beliefs: Blood is the only true currency. A wise lord never takes more than the herd can bear.
profile.relations: Profit from every baron's war; despise the Choir of Chains, whose dead have no blood; feared by the Plague-Beaks.
profile.war: Red Duelists with blood-blades; thralls as shields; night-beasts unleashed in desperation.
profile.trade: Blood-debts, castle rents and secrets bought at midnight.
npcs: Has offered to fight the Choir of Chains, for a price.
The finest swordswoman in the Marches, and bored with eternity.
Wants to be free and doesn't know how.
profile.weaknesses: Sunlight, silver, running water, holy ground.
quests: Negotiate (or refuse) Valcourt's price for fighting the Choir.
Help Gaspard break his thrall-bond.
profile.gameplay: A morally grey alliance option in the Strife Marches siege; freeing thralls is a side questline.

clans.name: The Whale-Singers
clans.look: Whale-folk, huge and gentle.
clans.culture: The singers who speak to Thalassa.
clans.hook: A Whale-Singer has heard another sand-whale singing.

profile.origin: The Whale-Singers are whale-folk who learned to speak to Thalassa when the first sand-whale towns were built. They are the only ones who can guide her, and the town would be lost without them.
profile.society: Singers led by the First Singer; barnacle-riders live closest to Thalassa's hide; spout-watchers keep lookout; calf-keepers remember the other whales.
profile.beliefs: Thalassa is mother and her song is the town's heartbeat. When she stops singing, the town will die.
profile.relations: Partners of the Plateback, respected by the town captain, terrified of Glassmaw.
profile.war: Sonic songs that stun and shatter glass, including Glassmaw's teeth.
profile.trade: Guiding the whale; songs sold to oasis towns.
npcs: Has heard another sand-whale singing, far away.
Watches for Glassmaw from Thalassa's Crown.
Remembers the other sand-whales and their songs.
quests: Find the other singing sand-whale.
Help Kel track Glassmaw's glass trails.
profile.gameplay: Whale-song steering of the moving town; sonic attacks crack Glassmaw's teeth.

clans.name: The Greyhowl Clans
clans.look: Wolf-folk in armour and cloaks, from wanderers to kings.
clans.culture: The wolfkin clans of the steppe, who trace descent through their grandmothers and follow the herds from pasture to pasture.
clans.hook: A wolfkin grandmother wants her grandchildren back from Kade.

kinds.name: Grandmother Packs
kinds.text: Clans led by their eldest women.

kinds.name: Moon-Howlers
kinds.text: Wolves who speak with the ancestors in the wind.

profile.origin: The Greyhowl Clans are the wolfkin of the steppe, who say their first grandmother was a wolf who learned to stand at the Wolf Stones. They follow the herds and trace their descent through their grandmothers.
profile.society: Clans led by their eldest women, the Grandmother Packs; Wind-Runners scout, Iron-Fangs fight, Moon-Howlers speak with the ancestors in the wind.
profile.beliefs: The wind carries the ancestors. The water-peace is holy, and Kade has broken it.
profile.relations: Allies of the Hoofbound, enemies of the Laughing Packs who serve Kade, kin to the yurt camps.
profile.war: Fast raids, coordinated pack tactics and iron-shod fangs.
profile.trade: Wool, felt, horses and hunting.
npcs: Wants her grandchildren back from Kade, and keeps the Howling Hearth in Fanghold.
The fastest scout on the steppe.
Hears the ancestors in the wind, and they are angry.
quests: Rescue Ruka's grandchildren from Kade's ledger.
Help Sairan hear what the ancestors want.
profile.gameplay: Main Fanghold faction; pack-tactic companions.

clans.name: The Snowmanes
clans.look: White-furred yetis, huge and shaggy.
clans.culture: Snowline dwellers who carry goods up the Long Stair for the Heavenfolk.
clans.hook: A Snowmane porter has seen Aquilon take a child.

kinds.name: Porter-Chiefs
kinds.text: Lead the porters of the Long Stair.

kinds.name: Stair-Carriers
kinds.text: Carry goods up eleven thousand steps.

kinds.name: Avalanche-Callers
kinds.text: Can start or stop an avalanche.

profile.origin: The Snowmanes are yetis of Heavenreach's snowline who have carried goods up the Long Stair for the Heavenfolk for generations, in return for honey, cloth and the right to live in the high meadows.
profile.society: Porter-families led by a Porter-Chief; Stair-Carriers do the hauling; Avalanche-Callers keep the slopes safe; hermits live alone above the clouds.
profile.beliefs: A load carried is a promise kept. The mountain gives way to those who listen to it.
profile.relations: Old allies of the Heavenfolk, friendly with the valley folk, frightened of Aquilon's rocs.
profile.war: Avalanches called down on enemies, great strength and thick fur.
profile.trade: Portering up the Long Stair, snow-honey and mountain herbs.
npcs: Has seen Aquilon take a child.
Can start or stop an avalanche with a single shout.
Lives alone above the clouds and talks to the rocs.
quests: Carry a load up the Long Stair with the Snowmanes.
Find the Hermit Above and learn what he knows about Aquilon.
profile.gameplay: Snowmane porters carry the player's gear up the Long Stair; avalanche allies in Heavenreach.

clans.name: The Warhorse Kin
clans.look: Horse-folk warriors and breeders.
clans.culture: Breeders of Vharlen's warhorses.
clans.hook: A Warhorse Kin breeder has a foal that can outrun demons.

profile.origin: The Warhorse Kin are horse-folk who have bred Vharlen's warhorses since the empire's founding, and they say the first emperor rode one of their ancestors into battle.
profile.society: Breeding families led by Grey Mares; Breeders raise the foals; Chargers form the heavy cavalry; Mustangs scout the wild plains.
profile.beliefs: A good horse is a good soldier, and a good soldier is a free one.
profile.relations: Partners of the Iron Legions, proud of their service and resentful of being treated as stock.
profile.war: Heavy cavalry charges that break demon lines; Mustangs harass and scout.
profile.trade: Warhorses, breeding and cavalry training.
npcs: Has a foal that can outrun demons.
Leads the heavy horse and has never lost a charge.
Free, fast and refuses to serve the legions.
profile.weaknesses: Rough terrain; being treated as property.
quests: Protect Equina's foal from demon raiders.
Ride with Brutus's cavalry in the next charge.
profile.gameplay: Ground warhorse mounts from Vharlen; cavalry charges in sieges.

guardians.name: The Verdant Lantern
guardians.role: Order of the Keepers of Life
guardians.text: A hidden order sworn to tend the Weave where it frays: healers, archivists and wardens who serve no kingdom. They know the Guardians exist and recruit those strong enough to meet them.

guardians.name: The Threshold Wardens
guardians.text: Armoured sentinels of the Keepers who stand at thresholds no one should cross: the Door at One-Twenty, the Root's Kneeling Stones, the Red Heart of Vesper. Each must be persuaded or defeated.

guardians.name: The Paragons
guardians.text: Rulers who stand above their clans: one paragon per great people (a lion-king, a dwarf High Thane, a Heavenfolk elder). In play, a recruitable 'clan champion' per region after liberation.

guardians.name: Aequis, the Twin-Weighted
guardians.text: Two figures in one, white and black, holding the scales of the Weave. Neither good nor evil; it fights whoever tips the world too far.

heralds.name: The Scale-Bearers
heralds.text: Twin monks, one white and one black, who never speak at once.

guardians.name: Nimbaros, the Waiting Titan
guardians.text: A titan of cloud and gold who walks the abandoned Titan cities, waiting for the Titans to return.

heralds.name: Nimbus Wardens
heralds.text: Cloud-shaped titans who patrol the floating bridges.

guardians.name: Carcinoth, the Island That Sleeps
guardians.text: An ancient crab the size of an island, sleeping under the reefs; the Krakenmother's oldest rival.

heralds.name: The Reef Choir
heralds.text: Coral crabs who tend the sleeping island.

guardians.name: Morwenna Ossaray, the Keeper of Count
guardians.text: A reaper of pale bone and black silk who keeps count of every soul that does not move on; the Mad Magician's show offends it.

heralds.name: The Countkeepers
heralds.text: Pale reapers who carry ledgers of names.

guardians.name: Sahrazet, the Glass Sphinx
guardians.text: A sphinx of glass and sand who asks one question and remembers every answer.

heralds.name: Riddle-Sphinxes
heralds.text: Lesser sphinxes of glass who guard the streaks.

guardians.name: Oakhaldr, the Antlered Deep
guardians.text: A mossy giant with antlers of living branches, asleep in the World Tree's roots beneath Mycelia's cave.

heralds.name: Root-Stags
heralds.text: Antlered spirits of the World Tree's roots.

guardians.name: Tuskaroth, the Grazing King
guardians.text: A great horned beast that every Calamity visits at the Tusks; perhaps it is what the Tusks belonged to.

heralds.name: Herd-Shepherds
heralds.text: Giant beasts who keep the Calamities moving.

guardians.name: Ignavor, the Walker Within
guardians.text: A burning figure with molten veins who walks inside the volcanoes; the monks' lullabies are partly for it.

heralds.name: Lava-Walkers
heralds.text: Burning figures who rise from the vents.

guardians.name: Selunae, the Silver Mourner
guardians.text: A pale, crowned lady who keeps the silver moon's light and mourns what the red moon takes.

guardians.name: Calliveth, the First Song
guardians.text: A singer whose voice made the first songs; the Drowned Choir is a twisted echo of her.

heralds.name: Echo-Singers
heralds.text: Spirits who repeat every song ever sung.

guardians.name: Rhimeheart, Warden of the Shattered Sky
guardians.text: A crystalline warrior at the Shattered Sky who keeps the world's winter in balance, and disapproves of Ymgrir.

heralds.name: Rime Knights
heralds.text: Crystalline warriors of the Shattered Sky.

guardians.name: Umbrask, the Elder Dark
guardians.text: A figure of living darkness in the deepest webs, older than the city; the Hollow Ones are its children.

heralds.name: The Eldest Hollow
heralds.text: The first of the Hollow Ones.

guardians.name: Aqualis, the Waterfall Serpent
guardians.text: A serpent of clear water who carries the great waterfall on its back.

heralds.name: Fall-Serpents
heralds.text: Water serpents who ride the waterfall.

guardians.name: Valoreth, the Golden Witness
guardians.text: A golden-armoured knight who appears on battlefields where both sides fight for something worth keeping.

heralds.name: Golden Witnesses
heralds.text: Knights who appear where battles matter.

fauna.name: Wart Bird
fauna.text: A heavy, flightless-looking bird that can glide short distances; herders use them as watch-birds.

fauna.name: Lantern Moth-Hawk
fauna.text: A moth-winged raptor that hunts by moon-glass light.

fauna.name: Feather Serpent
fauna.text: A winged serpent of the river-cities, sacred to the Eagle lodge.

fauna.name: Moorwah
fauna.text: A shaggy, long-snouted grazer; Frostveil's draught animal and a ground mount.

fauna.name: Shulon
fauna.text: A long-necked, llama-like climber used on the terrace roads; a ground mount.

fauna.name: Stone-Horned Ox
fauna.text: A ram-horned grazer that senses tremors; the Stillhorns' herds.

fauna.name: Saurian Longneck
fauna.text: A dinosaur-sized grazer with glowing spine plates; one of the steppe's giants.

fauna.name: Velvet Bee
fauna.text: A sparrow-sized bee with a furry body, the source of Mossdeep honey.

fauna.name: Plated Crawler
fauna.text: An armoured centipede that burrows in Thalassa's hide.

fauna.name: Thorro
fauna.text: A bear-like river predator that fishes the moonwells.

fauna.name: Ghost Fox
fauna.text: A pale, flame-tailed fox, maybe a spirit, maybe an animal.

fauna.name: Tingra
fauna.text: A lean, striped hunter of the mountain passes.

fauna.name: Whale-Roach
fauna.text: A many-legged, whale-sized crustacean that scavenges the floes.

fauna.name: Reef Dragon
fauna.text: A long, spiny sea-dragon that nests in the wrecks.

fauna.name: Turtle Drake
fauna.text: A shelled sea-drake that carries islands of coral on its back.
